speaker: The Chairman
text: Head X, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We are celebrating our 54th National day this August.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The task of nation-building is an endless one.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is one that needs all Singaporeans, regardless of race, language or religion, to come together, rally together as one united people and one nation.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We come together to celebrate every success Singapore achieves, to celebrate our uniquely Singaporean culture, food, arts and sports.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It only seems like not so long ago when young Singaporeans were thought to be politically and socially apathetic.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Yet, today, we have an increasingly mature citizenry with a diverse array of views and hopes for their own future, and for the future of Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: These can be attributed to a society with growing literacy and affluence, where they are able to take the focus off from bread-and-butter issues to other matters and issues that affect their lives.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The widespread use of social media certainly helps them and rallies them in expressing their views.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And the Government needs to do more to engage and partner Singaporeans in the next exciting phase of nation-building.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Our youths and our older Singaporeans who have found common ground have bandied together and created groups to promote their causes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: They participate in forums and focus group discussions.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: They are vocal on social media, some are more sophisticated with their analyses and feedback, others less so.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: But it is evident that many Singaporeans would like to have an active role in nation-building and shaping the future.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Some expressed their views through arts, music and culture.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: However, some are unsure of the available avenues, or lack the capability to do so.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Online feedback portals, community outreach events, facilitation of networking events for stakeholders and volunteers to come together are some examples of ways in which Singaporeans can engage in nation-building.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Nevertheless, the majority of the engagement feels top-down, in the sense that citizens provide feedback and the Government works on it.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: We need to move away from a top-down approach to a less paternalistic approach.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: The Government needs to create more space, room and opportunities for Singaporeans to participate.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: For those who are ready to do more, particularly Singaporeans with leadership qualities, good ethics and are socially well-connected, they should have more opportunities to participate.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: They could create social projects and lead teams of volunteers.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: For those who are not ready, perhaps they lack comprehension of policies, or skills to articulate their aspirations and feedback, and we must help them to grow their capability.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: This can be done through giving them access to the necessary information, and the skills to participate.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Many Singaporeans still find certain policies to be too complex to understand, and they do not get why certain policies have to be this way.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: If the Ministry could come up with more creative means to break down these policies for the layman, that would be helpful.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: It is prudent that all citizens in Singapore have a stake in nation-building, to ensure equality and for everyone’s interests to be cared for.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Our population has always been and will always be our best resource, and with a more well-informed population, there will be more and better possibilities.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: As we face more complex issues, we will be able to tap on the collective wisdom and expertise of our citizenry.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: As we build Singapore together, we can work towards creating the best Singapore that we can, one that all citizens have a stake in.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How can we raise the commitment levels towards building a Singaporean society where everyone can continue to be proud of our country and its achievements?

text: (In Malay):  :  First, I would like to wish a Happy Women's Day and a Blessed Month of Rejab.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: They are important in equipping generations of azatizahs with a firm foundation in both secular and religious subjects.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: These azatizahs are our community assets and we are very proud of them.

text: It is critical that we ensure madrasah students and teachers in Singapore continue to receive ample support and opportunities to fulfil their potential.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: What is being done to enhance our madrasahs so that they can continue to produce good quality graduates and continue their illustrious tradition?

text: First, what is the roadmap or strategic plan for M3?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, what are the mid-term and long-term objectives that have been outlined?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, what is the difference between M3 and the current collaboration between MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA before it was named M3, especially in their adopted approach to achieve the objectives that were outlined?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Fourth, what are the key values that we wish to inculcate and develop in the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: On several occasions, he quoted current and past renowned religious scholars as role models and sources of reference.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, at the same time, it is an obligation or responsibility of every Muslim, especially political and community leaders, to advise or counsel one another for any shortcomings or mistakes in our mission to further strengthen and uplift the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Together, we will strive and pray that the Malay/Muslim community will become a community of excellence, that calls us to perform good deeds and forbids us from doing bad things, as well as a community that provides guidance and leadership, instead of the other way around.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This would enable collaborations among the three organisations to be better coordinated, thus improving support from Government organisations, while streamlining the process for beneficiaries to seek assistance and resources.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a promising programme which not only seeks to educate children but also parents who want to help their children improve important skills.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What new projects and developments can we expect from M3?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Additionally, MENDAKI has some satellite centres around Singapore, including in some of the neighbourhood estates and the Institute of Technical Education (ITE) College campuses.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: These have enabled MENDAKI to conduct outreach in the heartlands and enabling more timely and accessible assistance.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As residential areas continue to evolve, can we also look forward to more satellite centres?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, may I take both cuts together?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to extend the warmest wishes of Rajab Shahrullah Mubarak to my Muslim colleagues here.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: And "Happy Women's Day" to all the female Members in the House.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Mr Chairman, last year, Minister Masagos Zulkifli announced the formation of M3, which includes MUIS, MESRA and MENDAKI.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: The spirit of M3 is one of working together.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: In this regard, it is important that our Malay/Muslim and Indian/Muslim community organisations are involved, as well as with other communities.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: In so doing, we fully tap on the assets in our community.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: The M3 institutions have extensive ground networks and community-based programmes which other communities could participate in and also partner.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Could the Minister share more about how M3 agencies could work with other community groups towards a common social cause?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: A significant of our returning religious graduates take on jobs in the religious sector in Singapore and form the core of our asatizah fraternity.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: It is important to engage them early, even while they are studying abroad, so that they are confident of their skillsets and future opportunities upon their return.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Could the Minister provide an update on MUIS' support for our overseas students?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Mr Chairman, since I have a bit more time, I would like to thank all the civil servants and all the officers who have been working behind the scenes to ensure that these COS proceedings have been going smoothly.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In Malay):   	I would like to wish everyone a blessed month of Rejab.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, every year, a sizeable number of each cohort of our madrasah students further their studies at the university level in Islamic tertiary institutions overseas like the Al-Azhar University in Egypt and the Jordan University.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many return to Singapore after graduation to serve in our community as Islamic teachers or asatizahs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, we recognise that there are a limited number of places for the employment of asatizahs in our mosques and madrasahs.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How can we also ensure that they will continue to be strongly rooted in Singapore’s multiracial and multi-religious context, so that their knowledge, teachings and influence remain relevant to our society and are effective in guiding our community amidst a more religiously and socially diverse landscape?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to seek an update on the previously announced plans for an SIC.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Where are we now in terms of establishing such an institution?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef, you can take both cuts together.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   	Singapore is increasingly being recognised as having a religious sector and religiosity that are organised and practical, with evidence-based fatwas and religious policies.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Our asatizahs and eminent experts on religion also help to support this reputation.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Many other secular countries with Muslim minorities want to learn about our model.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What about the programmes that will be made available, as well as courses that will be held?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Where will we acquire the teaching faculty from?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: These asatizahs comprise new graduates as well as those who have spent years in the religious sector and are highly experienced.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: They can and will have the potential to contribute immensely to the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore and globally.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How will MUIS provide support to them in terms of life-long learning, increasing their knowledge and other activities under this masterplan for asatizahs?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How will MUIS continue to support them as they discharge their roles in Singapore, perhaps the region as well, where they may be consulted and called upon?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: (In Malay):   	Our asatizahs are integral figures in guiding and shaping the beliefs of the Muslim community and, thus far, they have done well in their work.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Asatizahs can and should use their influence to reach out and contribute towards other communities’ needs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Hence, asatizahs who are thinking of exploring other opportunities to serve the community will also need to work towards achieving the relevant professional skillsets for such roles.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How will MUIS support asatizahs in these endeavours?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What other professional development award schemes can asatizahs tap on or use to develop their capabilities?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam, you can take both cuts together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   	Preschool education is crucial in preparing our children for primary school.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: However, there are still some in our community who are still unaware of its importance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some may feel that learning to read and write should only begin formally at primary school, and they do not give due attention to preschool education and preparing their children to enter Primary 1.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This has caused some children in our community to find it hard to follow the primary school curriculum and end up academically behind their classmates.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: MENDAKI has endeavoured to address this gap by providing specialised programmes to prepare parents and their children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Has this effort achieved its outcomes and have we seen any improvement in our young children’s performance?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Recently, issues touching on parents' responsibility in teaching their children were hotly discussed after a Facebook post by an adjunct teacher went viral.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I shall not discuss the post, but one important issue that came up was the role of parents in early childhood education and the ongoing efforts to help children in their development.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Perhaps some parents need a bit of guidance and help in this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I welcome MENDAKI's tireless efforts all these years to get parents to be involved in their children’s education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am confident that the continuous efforts by MENDAKI and our community in general will help us to keep improving our children’s performance and capabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   	Education is one way for us to transform the life of one generation into a better life.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: With education, one can acquire knowledge and skills, and also have a better chance to get a meaningful career and a good pay.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We are aware that we have to start education at a young age.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If we think about it, families that are more affluent can ensure that the child is well looked after even before being born.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The mother consumes nutritious food and this, in turn, ensures the baby is healthy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: After birth, the child continues to receive nourishment and begins to be exposed to all kinds of early educational materials.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: At preschool level, the child's capability continues to be developed.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: If we compare a child that has been exposed to early education and one that has not, there is clearly a difference.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is heart-breaking if a child is unable to receive certain advantages because of family background.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Therefore, it is important to ensure that all of our young have access to early education, regardless of family background or income.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In the Malay community, preschool is informally called makan school.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are those who sometimes do not care whether their children attend preschool or not.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is our community's responsibility to raise awareness about the importance of preschool education.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Community organisations, preschool education specialists and parents can work together on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What can be done with the community and the Government to increase awareness about these issues and to provide holistic support to help parents enrol their children into preschools?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   	I would like to wish a blessed month of Rejab to all Muslims and a Happy Women’s Day to all the ladies in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This programme aims at helping low-income families with preschool-going children to have a good foundation in education, especially in Mathematics.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In September last year, M3 committees in the various towns launched the KMM programme in Nee Soon, Marsiling and Pasir Ris.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: What are the plans to expand KMM to benefit more low-income families with preschool-going children?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: (In Malay):  :  Many of our young people have achieved success in their professions and made their mark in their careers and contributions to society.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Their stories of perseverance have been featured in mainstream media and social media.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Their peers and others in our community are proud of their achievements and see them as sources of inspiration.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: I am pleased that there are also a good number of them who care for others and have a strong desire to give back to the community.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We should tap on their energy and life experiences as well as empower them with opportunities and platforms to continue their good work and encourage others.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: How can we mobilise these individuals to contribute towards the development of our nation and community?

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, for decades now, MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA have individually nurtured our community's values, uplifted individuals and families through education and community self-help, and fostered our community’s participation in our larger multiracial society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, and in a structured way, M3 and with the vast energy of the Malay/Muslim community, we can help one another reach even greater heights.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition to the volunteers and staff of MUIS, MENDAKI and MESRA, M3@Town has also become a network for professionals to contribute in their local neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The KelasMateMatika@CC pilot was our first experiment to learn and get used to working together.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is important because we need to deliver joint M3 community projects which can be bigger.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In fact, this programme, KelasMateMatika@CC, was preceded or developed successfully during the leadership of my predecessor, Minister Dr Yaacob Ibrahim, during his leadership at MENDAKI.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Now that the synergy from the model of collaboration in KelasMateMatika@CC has achieved good initial results, we will scale up the M3 efforts to benefit more in the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Faisal Manap asked about the progress and plans for M3.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the next phase, M3 seeks to achieve the following.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, enabling our community, especially our young, to access educational and developmental opportunities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, fostering sound values that undergird our socio-religious life – values that reject extremism and segregation, and nurture an inclusive, confident and progressive mindset of caring for the common good of society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, providing opportunities for our community to bond with others over common causes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When we work with other communities, we become familiar with one another, deepen mutual understanding and trust, and forge friendships.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The M3 comprises circles of excellence in our heartland towns, tapping on assets in the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These are no other than committed and capable individuals who are willing to contribute time and effort to the community in a structured way and flexibly co-creating services suited to the needs of the areas they serve.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The soul of the M3 effort is about stepping forward and giving back.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The circle is formed by successful individuals helping others around them to see possible paths ahead and creating opportunities for the next generation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   	M3 begins as a virtuous circle of excellence.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A successful Malay/Muslim community must be anchored on strong local communities, drawing on the rich networks and relationships in our neighbourhoods and workplaces.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is where MESRA will focus its energy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: M3@Town will mobilise people and community as well as national assets in our towns, connecting residents to a more efficient and effective last-mile service delivery.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Community programmes will be brought closer to residents to increase residents’ awareness and participation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: M3@Town will also create opportunities for people, regardless of background and abilities, to volunteer and serve the people in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our Malay/Muslim People's Action Party (PAP) Members of Parliament (MPs) are leading efforts to establish M3@Towns.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They have brought the M3 agencies together in their towns and mapped out the needs, assets and community programmes at our Community Centres/Clubs (CCs), mosques and MENDAKI satellite centres.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They have also begun to mobilise volunteers across M3.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The launch of M3@Tampines and Pasir Ris-Punggol was the first step.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The success of M3@Town depends on members of our community who are our assets.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We call on them to come forward, in particular, those who hold positions of expertise, leadership and responsibility.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Regardless of whether you are teachers, Singapore Armed Forces personnel, Home Team officers, lawyers or professionals, including those from the healthcare sector, you have a wealth of experience that can inspire and encourage our young.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, your stories as "mentors" will inspire them to take the long view of where they wish to go, beyond the twists and turns of the road ahead.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The younger generation needs role models whom they can emulate.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: You have the ability to guide them on how to build professional networks and widen employment opportunities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: M3 has started to work with our community organisations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, eight Malay/Muslim organisations, including the Association of Muslim Professionals (AMP), the PMBM Scholarship Fund Board (LBKM) and the Malay Youth Literary Association (4PM), have collaborated to provide a one-stop service centre at Wisma Geylang Serai or Kurnia@WGS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have heard the concerns from the ground that those in need do not always know where to go.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Similarly, the Singapore Malay Teachers’ Union worked with M3 agencies to encourage their members to volunteer.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Teachers play a critical role at the M3@Towns, connecting schools to the community and reaching out to students beyond the classroom.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A group of successful lawyers have also come forward to organise legal talks called Tipah Tertipu under the SHIOK Series in December 2018 at Woodlands Galaxy CC.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They educated Malay residents on protecting themselves from scams.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Muhammad Imran Abdul Rahim is a young lawyer who volunteers at M3@Town.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He began volunteering in Woodlands in 2016, after realising that many residents faced legal issues but lacked advice.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He used his experience and worked with other young lawyers to hold legal talks and pro bono legal clinics for residents and help out with community events.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I hope that the examples of M3 collaborations across our community organisations and volunteers will give assurance to Mr Mohamed Irshad on the potential of M3 to help achieve common social causes.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Just as we call on more to step forward to volunteer, we will continue to work with community partners, such as voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs), professional groups and the Malay and Indian Muslim organisations, to tap on strengths and amplify synergies.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim queried on how our community organisations are nurturing our children.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A mindset of pursuing excellence must be established in our children from young.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It starts with nurturing the traits of initiative, resilience and a desire for learning and knowledge.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will be a month dedicated to celebrating knowledge and excellence, because the pursuit of knowledge is highly regarded and is a central part of the culture of our Malay community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Raikan Ilmu Month will start with the launch of a Heritage Gallery to commemorate the community’s journey in pursuing educational excellence.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will also capture MENDAKI’s history and honour our predecessors who had been involved in the founding of MENDAKI.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In conjunction with Raikan Ilmu, MENDAKI will partner M3 agencies to organise activities as part of this year’s MENDAKI Learning Festival, with activities for all age groups.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For instance, Jump Career Fairs by MENDAKI SENSE will cater to workers and professionals keen on career training and skills upgrading, while the Future Ready Marketplace aims to advise youths on careers and professional development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For preschoolers and their parents, PlayFest focuses on early childhood education and learning through play.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Learning Festival will also celebrate the achievements of our graduates through the Anugerah MENDAKI Awards ceremony.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad will share more on MENDAKI's many initiatives.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I would now like to touch on our religious life that has a profound impact on our community's values.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar respectively asked about plans to prepare our religious teachers, or asatizahs, for a changing world, and an update on the plans to develop an Islamic college in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our asatizahs of today and tomorrow are the guardians and guides of our community’s core values.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our aspiration is for them to reach the highest level of religious scholarship and leadership, contributing to our community in Singapore and beyond, especially in building up religious knowledge that is appropriate to guide a Muslim community living in harmony with other communities and the wider society.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With their grounding in both Islamic knowledge as well as secular subjects, asatizahs are well-placed to serve in many adjacent fields, such as social work, counselling, Islamic finance and law.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This committee comprises community and religious leaders, asatizahs and individuals with relevant professional expertise.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: COFA will co-create our vision of the "Asatizah of the Future" together with the community, and advance the thinking on the skills and competencies that our asatizahs will need to better serve the Singapore Muslim community in the future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the findings of COFA, we will be able to share more about the long-term plans for developing our asatizahs by the end of the year.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PCICS will replace the existing Islam in Context Programme today, and place greater focus on helping participants acquire work-relevant skillsets.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These initiatives contribute to our larger effort to prepare for an Islamic college in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Minister of State Maliki Osman will share more.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Amrin Amin asked about efforts to enhance our madrasahs, and Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim asked for an update on MUIS’ support for Madrasah Wak Tanjong.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our madrasahs are key components of a larger blueprint for developing asatizahs of the future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, we are strengthening our madrasahs holistically.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to conclude in English, please.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): I shared the story of Muhammad Imran Rahim, an everyday hero who inspires us.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: He said, “I can’t discount the number of people who helped me to get to where I am today.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we will build a Community of Success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to join my colleagues in wishing all our women colleagues and women out there a very "Happy International Women's Day", and acknowledge and commend them for all their significant contributions to our families, our society and Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, our asatizahs anchor our community to values and traditions in a rapidly evolving world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Equally, our community’s social and religious needs are changing, and for our asatizah to serve the community well, they must stay relevant and possess a strong grounding in religious knowledge and work-relevant skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Mohamed Irshad asked about support for our overseas students, and Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar asked how we can ensure that their teaching is relevant to our community when they return.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef and Mr Saktiandi Supaat were concerned about development opportunities for our asatizahs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thirdly, to guide plans for enhancing asatizah development, I will chair COFA, which Minister Masagos announced earlier, to engage the community for views on the desired skills of our asatizahs in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   	Chairman, studying overseas is not easy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Besides adapting to the curriculum, students need to adapt to the local culture and systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: At the same time, we also have to ensure their ties to Singapore remain strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As such, MUIS' Student Career and Welfare Office (SCWO) has deployed three SLOs, who mentor these students to help them keep abreast of Singapore’s developments and prepare them for future careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As alumni of the universities in the same regions, these SLOs are familiar with the environment and common issues our students face.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These three SLOs also support the overseas Singaporean student welfare groups, such as the Singaporean Students Welfare Assembly in Cairo, Singapore Students’ Association in Jordan, the Association of Singapore Students in Saudi Arabia and Association of Singapore Students in the International Islamic University Malaysia in Malaysia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The SCWO is ready to engage our students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Before the students leave, SCWO shares with them about the extra-curriculum opportunities, education and career pathways, and general information, such as finances and personal safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: When these students return to Singapore for their annual summer vacation, the SCWO engages them through various activities, such as workshops on contemporary Islamic thought, skills to improve their employability, internships and career coaching sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Upon graduation, the SCWO refers them to the Asatizah Recognition Scheme (ARS) Office and MUIS Academy for developmental programmes and further career coaching sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: What we want is that, with their qualifications, they receive the guidance that they require in order to be successful in their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of our SLOs is Ustaz Goh Muhammad Redhuan, based in Cairo, Egypt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Redhuan looks after about 300 Singaporean students in the Middle East and North-African region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He has supported them in university administration matters and initiated developmental programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, in December 2018, Ustaz Redhuan organised a learning journey for 60 students in Cairo to visit two synagogues there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The students had a fruitful discussion with Cairo's Jewish community, learning about the culture and traditions of the Arab Jew community, and dispelling their prior misconceptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In January this year, he arranged for a visit to the reputed Al-Azhar Observatory for Countering Extremism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Ustaz Redhuan's support, the students have also organised dialogues on current issues in Singapore and discussed possible ways for them to contribute to the progress of the community and the nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Intan Mokhtar asked how we are preparing our returning religious graduates with work-relevant skills and knowledge to serve our community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past two years of running ICON, MUIS has received positive feedback from ICON participants that not only has the programme been useful, but that the scope of the programme could be widened to include more work-relevant skillsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: PCICS will offer modules that deepen our returning graduates' understanding of our geopolitical and socio-religious context and how Islam can be practised effectively in our multiracial and multi-religious society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is important to prepare them for their role in providing religious guidance to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: PCICS will also equip participants with work-relevant knowledge and skillsets, such as in social work and counselling, digital literacy as well as entrepreneurship, to open up more opportunities for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Graduates of PCICS will also be recognised under ARS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Chairman, over the past week, Members of this House had reminded us of the various ways in which the world around us is changing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Geopolitical forces are evolving and shifting, the economy and its demands on Singaporeans are changing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Likewise, our religious landscape and social norms are also evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singaporean Muslims need to move with the times, in their professional and socio-religious lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COFA comprises members who have come forward to volunteer their services to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They include senior and younger asatizahs, leaders from the madrasah sector, community leaders, Muslim professionals, and individuals and academics with expertise in social work and continuing education and training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef and Dr Intan Mokhtar asked for an update on the development of an SIC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COFA's work is a critical step towards the college, because it will deepen our understanding of what the community desires of our future asatizahs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through these engagements, MUIS will be able to chart the holistic development of our asatizahs, from the madrasahs to the universities, and into their employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MUIS will also be able to map out the skillsets that our asatizahs will require to serve our community effectively and develop pathways for careers within and beyond the religious sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These findings will provide us with a strong foundation for establishing the SIC in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have a vision of a strong and vibrant religious sector that provides more opportunities for our asatizahs to serve the needs of our community as well as the broader society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our asatizahs must continue to stay relevant, given the complex and ever-changing environment that they are operating in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am confident that COFA’s engagements with the community will guide MUIS as it embarks on important initiatives to strengthen our religious sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, today, we have over 4,000 asatizahs who play a critical role in guiding the Singapore Muslim community in being part of a cohesive and multiracial society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking to the future, we have a vision of a strong and vibrant religious sector that provides more opportunities for our asatizahs to serve the needs of our community as well as the broader society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our asatizahs must continue to stay relevant, given the complex and ever-changing environment that they are operating in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am confident that COFA's engagements with the community will guide MUIS as it embarks on important initiatives to strengthen our religious sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, I wish to wish all our wonderful women Happy International Women's Day and also to all my Muslim friends Salaam Rejab.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, social mobility is a key feature of Singapore society, and education is central to enabling mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI has uplifted individuals and families through educational support, by supporting their development and mobilising wraparound support for both parents and children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To enhance school-readiness among our young, MENDAKI is focusing on early childhood education, informed by expert findings, and strengthening networks between parents and preschool professionals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With M3, it will also provide opportunities for role models in our community to contribute and inspire our young to greater heights of excellence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   	Mr Chairman, research has shown that language acquisition and development are most effective at younger ages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Enrolment and regular attendance at preschool are hence critical.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We want to raise awareness among families of the importance of preschool education and the need for regular attendance, and assist them in enrolling their children into preschool and related-MENDAKI programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam also spoke about the central role that parents play in their children’s early development, and we want to help them in their endeavour.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: At the same time, research has shown that play is important for child development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Hence, under MENDAKI's School Ready Campaign, MENDAKI pioneered PlayFest to encourage and support parents of preschoolers from age zero to six in adopting a play-based approach to develop their children’s reasoning skills, and in setting up a stimulating learning environment at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI also introduced PlayKit, to encourage parent-child bonding using household items for craft work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Five hundred PlayKit sets have been distributed to families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, more than 90 members of the MENDAKI Alliance of Preschool Professionals network had organised training sessions for volunteers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are encouraged by the parents’ receptivity, and MENDAKI will organise one PlayFest and two mini PlayFests in 2019.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We aim to grow this partnership with preschool professionals for parents to benefit from the latest educational techniques and research findings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, under the M³ framework, we are also strengthening programmes to raise our children’s preparedness for Primary 1.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zainal Sapari asked for an update on KelasMateMatika@CC based on MENDAKI's Tiga M programme which we launched in Nee Soon, Marsiling and Pasir Ris last September.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The past cohorts of Tiga M students have done well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through this, we see that Tiga M has helped strengthen the foundations for our children’s education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To build on Tiga M, the M3 agencies collaborated to develop the KMM@CC programme and I am heartened by the results.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The pilot batch of KMM@CC supported more than 170 parents and children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For the second phase of KMM@CC, we have seen strong enrolment rates, with more than 300 parents and children indicating their interest to join, especially at Marsiling and Keat Hong, where the programme has been over-subscribed by more than double.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Support from centres in Woodlands, Choa Chu Kang, Boon Lay and Admiralty is also encouraging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is a clear signal that parents see the value of KMM@CC in helping their children develop strong foundations in numeracy skills, and increasing parents' confidence of teaching Maths at home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last September, she attended KMM@Nee Soon with her daughter.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond KMM@CC, MENDAKI will enrol families into Parent Circles near where they live.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These Circles facilitate sharing between parents and educators, which helps to enhance their parenting skills and confidence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Beyond preschool, we also intend to support children in our schools who need help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, MENDAKI oversees a tuition scheme that caters to over 10,000 students.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) recently provided updates about Uplifting Pupils in Life and Inspiring Families Taskforce (UPLIFT).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will ensure that M3 will dovetail its efforts with UPLIFT so that, together, we can provide support for disadvantaged students and their families through regular outreach, engagement and referral to community-based programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, a culture of excellence is important to spur the next generation onward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: As they grow older, our young will benefit from advice and mentoring from the right role models.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In time, we hope that beneficiaries from this programme will pay it forward as peer mentors to other youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, it takes a village to raise a child.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: Chairman, my clarification is for Minister Masagos Zulkifli.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: (In Malay):   	Could the Minister explain how the eight towns mentioned earlier were selected by M3?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I have two questions for Minister Masagos Zulkifli.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: (In Malay):   	Minister, my first question is on Madrasah Wak Tanjong.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I am aware that, after the financial assistance was given to Madrasah Wak Tanjong by MUIS, the madrasah is now administered by two chairmen.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: My second question is related to what the Minister said earlier on the involvement of PAP Malay MPs in the planning for M3 planning.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Right now, there is just me, but, hopefully, there will be more in the future.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I ask this question because I feel that the Minister might be familiar with the idea of ikhtilaf which means diversity of opinions, whereby the presence of ikhtilaf in the community is considered to be a blessing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In Malay):    The committee in Madrasah Wak Tanjong is still newly established, so we should allow them to get used to working together, just like the M3, with MUIS ready to assist the madrasah and will be neutral.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is important and, with cooperation, we can build a stronger, better and more effective madrasah institution in Madrasah Wak Tanjong.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: After a few years, we hope we will build more trust.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because the funds allocated come from the community, it should be monitored so that, if we are queried, we know where the funds are located and their effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Am I open to involving Members from the Opposition?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think we could ask the same question whether we could involve Members from the Opposition in the duties of the People's Association or CCs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, in terms of purpose, if the Opposition’s purpose is to oppose and disagree with what we are doing, I think it is better for the Opposition to focus on what they think is good for the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And we can still work together in matters where we do not have to disagree.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Mr Chairman, can I ask my clarifications in Malay, please?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: (In Malay):   	I would like to direct my two questions to Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki Osman.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: First, how will COFA have an impact on our asatizahs who are already involved in the religious sector?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Second, may I ask for some details on PCICS?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: And do we have plans to involve lecturers or faculty members beyond the religious sector, as well as other practitioners, in the teaching of this certificate course?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: (In Malay):   	First, the question on whether we will continue to include asatizahs who are already involved in the religious sector, they will certainly be involved because they are the stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As I have mentioned in my speech earlier, COFA will engage all of our stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Since they continue to be involved in this sector, the future of asatizahs is also their future.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Hence, we would include them and get their feedback on how they view their own future.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Can we expand the current opportunities in the religious sector to help them in their careers and how can they use the opportunities provided by COFA?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: COFA would also like to see how we can enhance career opportunities for our asatizahs beyond the religious sector.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, in terms of concept, COFA would be engaging all levels of society and obtain their feedback.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For those who are already in the religious sector, we welcome their cooperation.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We would like to give them new hope as well.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: ICON is a programme for our graduates who recently returned from overseas.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We have this programme to ensure that they understand how they can practise and teach religion in the context of a society like Singapore.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: PCICS is an extension based on their feedback that they require even deeper content.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: That is why it was called Post-Graduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: What can we include in PCICS over and above what was in ICON?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: First, by working beyond the religious sectors, they will acquire new expertise, such as from the counselling sector, the social work sector, as well as the digital, finance or legal sectors, because many of them graduated from the religious sector or studied religion.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, we want to see how they can be incorporated or work beyond the religious sector.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Subsequently, these students will be channelled to the MUIS Academy, which provides the accreditation, because once they have undergone PCICS, they will receive the ARS accreditation.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Mr Chairman, I have three clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: In my interactions with people, they have mentioned that it is very Malay-centric.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: I welcome the move that the Minister mentioned that M3 wants to partner with all organisations, including Indian/Muslim organisations and so on.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: But how can we have people from the other groups – Chinese/Muslims as well as Indian/Muslims – feel welcomed to be also part of this initiative?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: When can we expect it to be up and ready?

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Thirdly, recently, I was involved in a talk with the South mosque cluster and during that interaction with the asatizah, they did mention that, previously in MUIS, there was to be a function that looks into Youth Development.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Now, I understand that there is an Asatizah Youth Network.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: But can we bring that youth functionality back so that we can have a youth focus in every single mosque that we have in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Inevitably, the Malays are the larger portion of our community and, therefore, inevitably also we have to give them as much focus, in fact, proportionate focus.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But it does not mean we will leave anyone else behind.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We look forward to Indian Muslim Associations and other associations that are in line with us to support the development of our communities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, I am very happy to hear that the Indian/Muslim community feel a little bit left out, that they think that they are not part of the efforts, but they certainly are.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As for SIC, we do not want to pre-empt the need to understand what we need in the building blocks towards establishing SIC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to engage the asatizahs, we have to engage the community and, indeed, that is why COFA has been formed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: COFA will form the first building block towards the establishment of an SIC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But, like the Member and myself, we look forward to the establishment of SIC.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Lastly, on youth development, it does not really matter in what form it takes in the mosque, organisation or the support for it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We all know how important youths are and we certainly will not neglect them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Chairman, my question is for Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I just want to say that the efforts that we do for the Malay/Muslim community is really with regard to trying to make sure that we succeed with other Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Malay/Muslim is part of the bigger Singapore, and I am so happy to hear that we are also aligning with the efforts of UPLIFT.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I just wanted to check what are the other ways in which we are ensuring that the MENDAKI efforts are also being kept in line with national programmes, national key performance indicators so that we are also on par and also working towards the same goal overall in the country.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Indeed, many of our programmes are targeted at some of the challenges that we face in the community.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, for example, KMM was something we look at.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: When we look at where MOE is headed, preschools have shown to be one area we need to look at because many of our kids end up over-represented when they go into the Learning Support Programme and Learning Support Facilitator.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But after that, we managed to align it together with the other national programmes so that we can also tap on the expertise as well resources at the national level, so it goes both ways.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Another aspect in which we are also helping youths would be things like Future Ready, to prepare them for work-life ahead.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Apart from that, how we provide holistic care for families, there are also other areas in which we are working on.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But not just on our own but also through M3, the CCs, with MESRA and the wider MUIS and the mosques.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, there is a lot of scope now with M3 in place to leverage our resources at both the community and national levels.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, it is not a mutually exclusive thing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is both ways to address challenges of the community but leveraging the national resources.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Chairman, I have got a follow-up clarification to either the Minister or Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: With regard to the satellite centres, those mentioned in my cut, would there be plans to expand even further in terms of satellite centres in Singapore because the satellite centres that have been introduced are quite useful for the community and what are the timeline and plans for the satellite centres in the future?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to answer in Malay.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Mr Chairman, in recent times, around the world, we had seen disputes between people from different religions and races which resulted in major riots and conflicts that caused the loss of lives, casualties and much destruction.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Race and religion are one area which is often targeted for exploitation by groups and individuals for their own agenda, sometimes political and at times personal.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: They promote their fanatical views, stir up emotions and capitalise on those who are ill-informed, gullible or just to those who are already harbouring ill thoughts against our society.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The Singapore Government has done well as various agencies among the Ministries work together to address this matter collectively.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: There are many visits and events organised for their representatives and members to visit the various places of worship.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: All these promote better appreciation and understanding among the different religious faiths.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: But we are constantly bombarded by divisive elements which would deliberately misinterpret their religious teachings for their own ill intents.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have people with different religious beliefs coming here as visitors and workers, too.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How do we further strengthen the fabric of our society and promote interfaith harmony and peace in Singapore?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The news media has continually highlighted events where the lives of the ordinary people are disrupted because of violent acts carried out by terrorist groups in other countries.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have been fortunate to thwart several attempts by radicalised individuals from putting their intentions into action, but we must not let down our guard.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The main intention of such terrorist acts is to disrupt society, create chaos and distrust among the groups in our population.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Singaporean youths are passionate about shaping and contributing to social causes.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: From the environment to animal welfare, to welfare for the needy and to the plight of refugees in other countries, our youths have a wide array of interests.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Many have created their own community projects to support the causes they believe in, and they are also influencing their peers to do the same.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It is good to see our youths being motivated and taking an active stand to make a difference to their community.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: This ground-up approach would ensure that young citizens play a key role in effectively identifying and addressing their concerns, while the Government takes a supportive role.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We must harness this energy to do good and support our youths in their endeavours.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have platforms like the Youth Corps to match volunteers with the causes, be it on an ad hoc or regular basis.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Some of these projects are undertaken as co-curricular activities at our IHLs.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Can MCCY work with IHLs to further help and develop students through meaningful projects supporting social causes?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How is MCCY supporting our youths in this aspect?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Making our past known to our people is important if we are to help our people to understand the present.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The interaction between society and the past cannot be delinked because it has an unending relationship.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have many great leaders who have written or shaped the history of this country.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The history they wrote would teach us many lessons about our identity, our aspirations and about the warning signs that we have to heed.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: History, for example, has helped us to heed the warning signs of disharmony.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Hence, we are able to navigate ourselves successfully thus far on issues relating to racial and religious harmony, having learnt the consequences from past events.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: This year, we are celebrating our Bicentennial year.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It is important that we take this opportunity to share our rich history, the struggles, hardship and pain that our forefathers, our grandparents and parents went through.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How did we overcome the challenges of the British pullout from Singapore which, in turn, later gave rise to the birth of our Armed Forces and National Service?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Then how we went from self-government to Independence and the signing of the Separation Agreement and the Water Agreement, which is guaranteed by both the governments of Malaysia and Singapore.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: And how we aspire to safeguard our water security leading to our building of more water catchment areas, the venture into desalination and the birth of NEWater.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: How are we focusing on promoting our values and history and how are we engaging Singaporeans and taking our shared values to the next stage of development?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Today, we have SG Cares, which is a national movement to promote giving and kindness, and encourage a more caring society.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: This is good and we have seen how, through volunteering, neighbours get to know one another, friendships are cultivated among strangers from all walks of life and our society becomes more inclusive, and how we are able to muster support from various organisations, both from the public as well as private sectors, to be involved in this whole exercise.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Many companies now embrace corporate social responsibility (CSR) as part of their culture.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: At the heartland estates, there are more ground-up activities.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We see volunteers delivering porridge, free food to needy residents.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Mr Chairman, although we are a young country at 54 years old, we are not a cultural desert.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We have our own artforms from the different ethnic groups and our fusion forms, which we should showcase and promote not only at home but also overseas.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Our arts and culture reflect who we are and what we stand for as a nation to the rest of the world.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: It also brings us pride and recognition, as we showcase our cultural talents and capabilities to the world.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The richness of our cultures from all races is something that we should be able to promote abroad to draw tourists to our country as well.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Visitors come here to see modern buildings but also to soak in local arts and culture which are our strategic national resource.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: We should do more to project Singapore's soft power abroad.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Their works have unique Singaporean flavours that one will not find anywhere else.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The foreign exposure would help them to grow even more, so that they can become even better artists on their terms and realise their dreams.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What plans does NAC have to achieve these goals?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What has MCCY been doing to promote our cultural assets and talents overseas?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What are some of the key international initiatives that have been implemented over the years to help our local artists develop in terms of exposure and talent?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I always say we are so blessed to be living in Singapore where ladies are well respected and treated fairly.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This is a laudable goal to aim for, and I believe it can come to fruition through a combination of various factors.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As citizens of Singapore, we all take responsibility for our lives and actions.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The Government does not believe in giving handouts and it is the civic duty of citizens to help the less fortunate in our country.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As it is, the benefits of volunteerism are manifold.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: It is a source of significant contribution to the global economy.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Apart from economic contribution, volunteerism also enhances social connections between different sectors, and builds bridges across governments, enterprises and employees.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: It encourages citizens to be more active in civic engagement and mindful of their role in society.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Positive effects on volunteers as individuals includes increased self-esteem, enhanced emotional skills and capacities, expansion in career paths and an overall healthier physique and mentality.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: However, there are various influencing factors at play in Singapore which reduce the take-up rate of volunteering.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Chief among these is the reason that citizens have no time to volunteer.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: They fail to understand that giving to others does not mean having less time for oneself.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As a result, fewer are giving up their time and effort to volunteer for a good cause, even though donations are substantial.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As Singapore faces an ageing population crisis, it is even more crucial that youths are being engaged to volunteer with the elderly population.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: So, this begs the question: how can we further encourage the increase in number and depth of volunteerism in our nation?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: This draws from a large pool of ageing population with longer life expectancy, who are highly educated, active and financially secure.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: They are also proven managers of people, finances and complex programmes, who understand the benefits of meaningful work and are motivated to contribute to society.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The knowledge, experience and energy that these leaders bring represent a significant potential resource for the non-profit and charitable sector.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The result is a win-win situation which benefits both the community and retired leaders themselves, as volunteers generally enjoy improved health and wellness in the form of personal accomplishment and lower levels of depression.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: To attract these leaders, I would like to propose a two-pronged approach.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: An effective way is to locate and extend a personal invitation to leaders who are retired or will be retired in five years' time.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
