text: The second approach would be to design suitable volunteering opportunities.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: We should create awareness of the complete range of volunteering opportunities offered and then ensure that volunteering opportunities have specific targets and deliverables.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Volunteers would be more attracted to activities with clear job descriptions, well-defined expectations and timelines.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Short-term volunteering opportunities can also be offered to those with competing interests and limited available time.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Nevertheless, the most important aspect of attracting any form of volunteers will inevitably start with us.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: We, as leaders of the nation, are duty-bound to lead by example and be a visible beacon on the frontlines.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Only after being volunteers ourselves can we be exemplars and speak with passion about the great joy volunteerism can bring, in order to galvanise fellow citizens to be authentic volunteers.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Personally, I have been a pharmacist volunteer at a local hospice for the past 20 years.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Our volunteer pharmacists take turns every Saturday to visit the institution to sort out medication waste and monitor inventory of medications.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: On the days when it is my turn, I will bring along one of my four children to help out.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I task them to perform the "first cut" expiry date stock check while I sort out bags of medication waste for appropriate disposal and check on stock levels to trigger ordering.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: The aim is to attempt to engage them from young to appreciate the spirit of volunteering, though I will still recheck after them.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: At the end of our duty, as we walk along the corridor on our way out, I will ask my child to "peek" into a patient's room.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: I explain to them how the two hours spent earlier has helped to ensure that these terminally ill patients do not run out of essential medications, and are not taking expired drugs which may affect their pain control, vomiting or infection.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Ensuring appropriate disposal of these medications also has significant impact on protecting our environment and the safety of our residents.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Seeing the patients comfortable in bed during their last days can be especially emotional and underscores the heartfelt importance of the work that we are doing.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: And this is what has kept me going for the past 20 years as a volunteer.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: As a community leader and a mother who wants my young children to espouse the values of volunteerism, it also starts with us as leaders to shape the roads for successive generations to follow.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to leave Members with a quote from MK Gandhi: "The best way to find yourself, is to lose yourself in the service of others."

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As deep as the hurt, as great the loss, we must not forget why we suffer them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When the founding generation pledged themselves to build a strong Singapore Armed Forces, they were fully conscious that a strong military is only possible with fully committed National Servicemen drawn from every family in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They knew the costs and sacrifice that would be required.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Not only in resources that we invest in at every Budget, but much more precious would be the time, the sweat, the tears, even the lives of precious sons." Sir, the Founders' Memorial will be built to honour Singapore's founding generation of leaders by expressing the ideals and values upon which our nation is built.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: National Servicemen and regulars who lost their lives in training and on duty paid the ultimate price for these ideals and values.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The founding generation of leaders knew these sacrifices would be required to defend these ideals and values.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We must not forget the loss of these precious sons so that we can remember why we suffer the loss.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In one training course I attended a few years ago, my unit visited the Kranji War Memorial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Though I have been to the Memorial before, it was different visiting it in uniform and reading the Indian, Malay and Chinese names of soldiers who died defending Singapore on the wall of the Memorial.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It gave material meaning to our values and stirred in me the resolve to defend our nation.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These were men who died long before our nation was founded.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What more would the names of our precious sons who have fallen to defend our nation do to make us stand strong and united as a people.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Raising diversity in social ties is a collective effort.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: We have to encourage Singaporeans to take up opportunities to interact and make friends with people outside of their usual circles centred on a common race, language, religion, educational and housing background.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
text: Government agencies and community leaders can also do more to create the structures and programmes that encourage such mixing.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, we live in a pluralistic world, and Singapore, perhaps more than any other country, defines this measure.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With diversity comes the vibrancy of our community life – different religious groups celebrating festivals, intermingling of communities and living together in harmony.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With diversity also means that fault lines are never too far from the surface, which is why Singapore has always been careful in ensuring that these fault lines do not rupture.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must, first, recognise that when we talk about religious harmony in Singapore, it is not just skin deep.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have not achieved the harmony simply by talking about how similar we are.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: All religions, after all, aim for the good of Man, and also acknowledging that we do have differences and accepting those differences.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As the society becomes more affluent, correspondingly, a sizeable number also turn to greater religious life to find meaning to their lives.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Having been involved in inter-religious dialogue, I am proud that Singapore is often cited as an example of how we can be diverse, yet undivided.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How do we promote our way of religious harmony and also learn from the examples of others in challenging the issues of identity politics?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Like many Singaporeans, I go to my place of worship regularly.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Every Sunday, in church, I see large crowds of fellow believers gathering throughout the entire day.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In our mosques, our Muslim brethrens throng for Friday prayers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Temples are packed during key festivals as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We often go about our worship without much thought for safety or security.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet, we only need to look around us in the region to realise how starkly that religious organisations are obvious soft targets for terrorist attacks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must always engage one another in dialogue.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But it is in showing and experiencing our care for one another that we can truly have harmony.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to declare my interest as an athlete and take this chance to suggest how we may advance by optimising the resources that have been committed to sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: When I was five years old, I saw my brothers learning to swim at the pool.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Back then, I already had my condition and needed leg braces to assist my gait.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: But seeing how much fun my brothers were having, I asked my parents if I could join them and learn how to swim.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Back then, persons with disabilities in sports were nearly unheard of and it was almost 20 years early for inclusion to become the buzzword it is today.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Disability Sports Council, the charity that was tasked to offer a wide range of sports at both elite and non-elite levels, had only then hired its first two staff.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: On hindsight, it probably took a lot of guts for my swim coach then to take on a student with disability.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: But if not for her courage to include me, I may not be here today.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: But out of close to 100 swim clubs in Singapore today, I can count the number that have opened their doors to persons with disabilities in five seconds.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I hear stories from my peers on how they started in swimming, which can almost be considered a national sport for our little island.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Parents are spoilt for choice on whom they can engage to coach their children.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: But for parents of children with disabilities, it is a different story altogether.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Not every child has been as fortunate as me to meet a coach that brave.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Not many will be, if we do not set out to make changes.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Public efforts in raising awareness of persons with disabilities have been increasing.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Most, however, target individual transformation – of one to do their part to create a more inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The outcomes, therefore, depend heavily on the individual's own effort to accept this change.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: One, the individual is convinced; and two, the individual is not.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Let us take the first scenario where the individual is convinced, and ready to make a change.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Are our systems prepared to support such a change?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: On the second scenario where the individual had not been convinced, are we ready to let it go, or can we create an environment to motivate that transformation further?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If we have neither the systems nor the environment, then the probability of the returns on our investment would likely drop.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It is thus rather compelling to look at how we can boost our returns.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Can inclusion be scaled up beyond the individual and into the system?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I will go back to the context of sports with which I am most familiar with.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: What Sport Singapore (SportSG) has done is commendable.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Since the 2000s, SportSG has increasingly opened its doors to support athletes with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In the last two years, SportSG has also started to recognise coaches of disability sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Today, with all the evolution that has taken place in Singapore over the years, all that SportSG and SDSC have done, I am given the chance to be here.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: So here, I voice my dream of a Singapore where sports is a united front for Singaporeans, not separated into disability or able-bodied sports.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: It is a dream that already has ground globally, and one that I hope Singapore will join in.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Where the Paralympic Games benefit from the same standards in venues, infrastructure and planning as the Olympic Games, the Olympics benefit from the added layer of inspiration generated by the Paralympics.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The benefits have also been noticed down the chain.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: More International Sports Federations have or are beginning on paths of integration, like World Sailing and Union Cycliste Internationale.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Further down, countries like the United Kingdom (UK), Australia and New Zealand have also adopted integrated models for their national sports strategies.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Coaches and administrators are starting to realise that the spirit is the same amongst athletes, regardless of the number of limbs they have or whether they can speak.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: A swimmer who is intellectually impaired may need a little more instruction, but they still have to swim the right strokes, be the most efficient and be the fastest to win, similar to someone without intellectual impairment.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In the UK, disability sport is part of the National Sporting Associations.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The results of athletes with disabilities bring glory and funding to the Association equally as athletes without.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Funding benefits aside, integration promotes the sharing of knowledge and expansion of expertise.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Athletes have a chance to perform better with deeper expertise, while communities develop greater understanding and respect for one another.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The means might be different, but the spirit is the same.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: In spite of the different events we compete in, we share commonalities.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: The sporting scene in Singapore has been growing steadily in the past years.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Both able-bodied sports and disability sports have produced results and they continue to inspire the nation.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I believe it is now timely to discuss how to use this inspiration to transform our systems and forge an environment that complements other efforts of inclusion.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Holding up an important pillar of this environment is our National Sports Associations, also known as NSAs.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: By representing all athletes with disabilities through the Singapore Disability Sports Council instead of the sports they play, are we not putting the disability before the ability?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If an agency is representing a sport nationally, should it represent the sport to everyone in the nation, or only to those it deems fit?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: I believe a systemic transformation will motivate and complete individual transformation.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If an NSA is ready to make such a change, let us have our system ready to support it.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: If an NSA is not ready, then let us see how we can build an environment to better that probability.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Countries paraded the opening ceremony in their respective contingents, representing one nation and one dream.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: And he told me that the greatest moment of that Games was recognising the universality of the medal he received.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: There were no differences: only athletes brought together by a common spirit.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: And the medal reflected that: if you looked at it, you could not tell if it was given to a para-athlete or an able-bodied athlete.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: You were an athlete, and that was enough.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Local disability sports have started to pilot this transformation over the past few years.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: How can we bring this transformation to a larger environment and help NSAs embrace similar changes?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Most people are scared of change as a concept, but if we examine it, there are more things in sport that bring us together than separate us, more things to celebrate than to fight over.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: Let us use these commonalities to move forward, and not let hurdles of small differences, like different technical rules or different equipment, block our view of the finishing line.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: How can we help the NSAs to embrace this commitment?

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As an athlete, I am very grateful for all the resources that have been committed to sport.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
text: As a Singaporean, I hope that we can include the agenda of integration into our investments, so that they can give us not only returns on the individual, but for Singapore as a progressive nation.

text: Chairman, CSR has become an integral component in many organisations.

text: Mr Chairman, over the last decade, Singapore’s athletes have made steady progress on the international sporting scene.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Our female table tennis team did well in the 2008 Beijing Olympics and 2012 London Olympics.

text: Today's youths are passionate about many important national and international issues and are strong proponents of cause-based advocacy.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: They want to have a voice in policymaking and aspire to be heard.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: In Singapore, the Youth Conversation was kicked off last April for youths in Singapore to voice their concerns and aspirations about policies and causes in a safe space.

speaker: Mr Darryl David

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: What are the key themes that have emerged and what are MCCY's plans to deepen engagement with youths who have participated in these conversations?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Chairman, can I take my three cuts together?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Mr Chairman, we are living through rapid and profound societal changes in how we work, live, communicate and perceive reality.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Traditional hierarchies are being replaced by networks with multiple connections.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: People now behave more autonomously, shaped by a greater sense of individuality.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, it is not surprising that our youths today have aspirations and values that may differ from those of the previous generations.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: From what I have observed, our youths take a keen interest in not just issues that concern their future from education and employment, but to broader issues like climate change and environmental sustainability.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Our youths also want their views to be heard and to be taken into account in policymaking.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Some of our more passionate and proactive youths want to be involved, here and now, in coming up with solutions, and perhaps even implementing these solutions for the benefit of our people.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As our youths are our future, we need to tap on their youthful energy and enthusiasm.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We must also empower them to shape the future, which is very different from today.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, MCCY's efforts to encourage youths and engage youths must make sure that they can participate meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: As we reached the halfway mark, we see many successes.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: We have the established and well-loved icons from the National Gallery of Singapore to the Botanic Gardens.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: A new generation of musicians represents Singapore on the international stage, from Wong Kah Chun for classical music, to Joanna Dong for pop music, At the same time, both Singapore and the world have changed dramatically over the past decade.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, it is heartening that MCCY meets these challenges head-on through the 2018 Our Singapore Arts Plan, which recognises that arts do not just inspire and express the Singapore spirit.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Art can also bring diverse communities together and bridge societal fault lines.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: In a world that is increasingly fluid, our arts heritage anchors our national identity and inspires us to collectively adapt to the changing world.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
text: Therefore, can MCCY share on, moving forward, how the insights from the Arts and Culture Strategy Review as well as how our Arts Plan and our Singapore Heritage Plan will collectively shape our arts and culture sector?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: When we think about diversity and inclusiveness, most of us would associate these two words with workplaces where we encourage companies to embrace differences and to create a conducive work culture where people of different races and creeds and of different abilities are able to work alongside one another without fear and prejudice.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Creating a diverse and inclusive society requires more than fashioning conducive workplaces as people spend a majority of their time away from work.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The ideals of inclusiveness must thus be embedded within our social fabric where people of different abilities are able to live, work and play together.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: One aspect of inclusiveness that remains under-explored is how we could potentially use our "play" time to foster better understanding among people with different abilities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Can we leverage sports to build a more inclusive society, especially among those who have limited interactions with others different from themselves?

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: They make us what and who we are, shape our society and unite our communities, giving us a unique place in the world.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Beyond this, our heritage serves as an anchor when we are beset with challenging issues that may polarise our communities.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: As our founding Prime Minister observed of Heritage: "It… shapes the ways a people meet new challenges and helps them adapt and to survive." It is, indeed, good that we have entered into conversations with Singaporeans of all ages and backgrounds to discover what to them is significant as our intangible culture, what resonates with them and makes us singular and special as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Our music, literature, languages, stories, myths and folklores, rituals, customs, beliefs, practices, festivals and, of course, food must be considered, alongside other aspects with our special Singapore stamp and spin.

text: It is a culture that helps to reinforce our sense of national pride.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Chairman, today being International Women's Day, I would first like to thank our Members before me for your well wishes and also take a moment to acknowledge the achievement and the contributions of Singapore women to our families, to our society and to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And to all my sisters, Happy International Women's Day.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Since MCCY was formed six years ago, our cultural, community, sports and youth sectors have grown more vibrant.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are a strong society, built on firm foundations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Geopolitics and extremism threaten to unsettle the peace and stability we enjoy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At home, our population is ageing, while our youths have diverse aspirations, different from past generations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Business, work and daily life are being disrupted by digital technology.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These challenges are real and can fracture our society if not addressed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this complex world, we need new ways of working together, partnering one another to create innovative solutions and building trust.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In recent years, the Government has been engaging citizens, corporates and communities more deeply and extensively, to consult, co-create and co-deliver on issues that Singaporeans feel strongly about.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the economic front, we have seen many fruitful partnerships.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to partner investors and corporates to grow more local businesses.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the environmental front, we are reaching out to citizens and corporates to make a decisive shift towards sustainable lifestyles and practices.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have started building such partnerships via MEWR's 2018 "Year of Climate Action" and will work with citizens and industry to take collective action for 2019's "Year Towards Zero Waste".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the security front, more Singaporeans are playing their part as we expand the Community First Responders Network to mobilise and support those with relevant skills to help in emergencies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As the nature of national security evolves, the Government will work with businesses, schools and cybersecurity practitioners to strengthen our sixth pillar of Total Defence – Digital Defence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the social front, the Government is partnering VWOs, Family Service Centres and other community bodies, to strengthen support for students from disadvantaged families, and facilitating ground-up movements to grow their strengths and interests.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Businesses are stepping forward to provide employment opportunities for marginalised groups.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we harness the talent and creativity of our citizens to achieve more together, we can build a more inclusive Singapore that is home for everyone.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And in speaking to Singaporeans, I know many want to contribute to making Singapore our best home.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And this is the heart of MCCY's work – building together with Singaporeans a home that we care about and feel proud of.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We build a better home and grow together as a nation by creating community spaces for social interactions, designing programmes that create shared experiences and promote mutual understanding, and encouraging Singaporeans to pursue the common good.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Meanwhile, digital platforms, like giving.sg and the SG Cares app have helped connect hundreds of thousands of volunteers and donors to more than 500 charities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The year 2018 was a busy one for our athletes who, once again, flew Singapore's flag high at various major games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Team Singapore fielded 323 athletes across the 21st Commonwealth Games and 18th Asian Games, winning a total of 31 medals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This was followed by Team Singapore's best ever away performance at the 3rd Asian Para Games in Jakarta, with a medal tally of three golds, two silvers and five bronzes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Developments on the cultural front have also been encouraging.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In 2017, we saw record highs, with more than 11 million attending non-ticketed arts and culture events, and 5.4 million visiting national museums and heritage institutions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singaporeans were also able to enjoy over 9,500 performing arts activities throughout the year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Eight in 10 Singaporeans agree that Singapore is a caring and cohesive society and are satisfied with race and religious relations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: According to our 2018 Sports Index Survey, 64% of Singaporeans developed a stronger bond with people of different backgrounds by watching or participating in sports, an increase over 2017.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: More than seven in 10 are proud of Singapore's culture and heritage, with over 90% proud to be Singaporean.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about our plans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, MCCY will make partnering Singaporeans a focus of our work, and we will do so in the following ways.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And fifth, in realising the benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As announced during Budget 2019, SG Cares is a major undertaking of my Ministry.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SG Cares brings out the spirit of giving inherent in our DNA, making it a way of life for all of us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It starts with helping those around us, be it in our neighbourhood, school or workplace.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, we will be providing more resources and platforms to facilitate this as we build on our corporate, youth and senior volunteerism initiatives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will identify community-based organisations across Singapore to take on the role of Volunteer Centres (VCs).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These VCs will recruit, manage and develop volunteers on a sustained basis, create volunteering opportunities based on local needs, and build partnerships with stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In Bedok, Filos Community Services will be developing a volunteer engagement toolkit and framework to engage the stakeholders in Bedok to promote active volunteerism in the town.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In Jurong East, Loving Heart Multi-Service Centre has kickstarted "Neighbour Cares", a programme to mobilise neighbours as volunteers to look out for lonely seniors who need befriending services.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We recognise the value in mobilising the strengths of communities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the long term, we hope to grow "Neighbour Cares" in different neighbourhoods, where residents connect with and look out for one another with the help of the VCs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked if the VC initiative will be extended to more towns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Thereafter, we will review our progress before expanding our efforts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In Mandarin):   Last month, I came across a forum letter in Lianhe Zaobao, titled "Do not forget kind deeds just because they are small", written by Mr Zheng Zhaorong.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He said that while the large-scale programmes under SG Cares have served the community well, it is important to continue to perform small acts of kindness to one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Besides supporting Singaporeans to participate in more volunteer work in order to help the needy groups, we should also pay more attention to people around us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The spirit of care is often shown from being observant and from thoughtful acts of kindness.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In his letter, Mr Zheng thanked a young Singaporean who helped him pick up a coin he had dropped while buying a drink.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As the Mandarin saying goes, "do not do bad deeds just because they are minor, also do not forget kind deeds just because they are small".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Acts of kindness come in all forms and sizes, and this is the spirit of "SG Cares".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I hope Singaporeans will continue to show this spirit of care as we partner citizens in building a more caring society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In English): Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about our support for youths in contributing to social causes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will partner IHLs to help students transitioning from secondary school keep up their community involvement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will begin first with our polytechnics, ITE and universities before progressively expanding to all IHLs and some Private Education Institutes in the near future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Participants will go through a camp where they can meet like-minded, passionate youths, access YCS' networks and receive community leadership and skill-based training.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These youth leaders will catalyse more volunteer projects as they galvanise their peers to join them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They can tap on the National Youth Fund and Young ChangeMakers Grant for funding support.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By supporting their development as community service leaders and helping them build bonds with the communities they serve, we are hopeful that our youths will continue their volunteering journey even after they leave their institutions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Similarly, we will work with companies to incorporate senior volunteerism into their pre-retirement planning programmes, to encourage more seniors to volunteer.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Government will also take the lead in volunteerism through Public Service Cares, as part of the SG Cares movement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Senior Minister of State will provide more details on this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Next, cohesion – fostering mutual understanding and trust.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In a diverse society like Singapore, it is important that we continue to build mutual trust and understanding in pursuit of the common good.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We cannot take for granted the harmony we enjoy in Singapore and the sense of shared future we feel as one people.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our partners contribute to growing a more cohesive society in different and important ways.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They bring with them much needed capabilities, for instance, in consensus-building and interfaith and intercultural dialogue.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Alex Yam and Dr Lim Wee Kiak spoke about interfaith harmony.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In 2017, we launched BRIDGE, a series of community-driven initiatives, to foster better understanding and appreciation of the diverse religions and cultures in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In particular, the "Ask Me Anything" series, which is a platform to learn about different faiths, has seen a high degree of interest, with some 80% attendance from first-timers at each session, while more than 90% of participants indicated that they gained a better understanding of different faiths.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through this series, we have also seen more people indicating interest to be facilitators of interfaith and intercultural dialogues.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to work with our community partners to expand BRIDGE, as well as involve different segments of society in nurturing racial and religious harmony in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Given the important role our partners play, we will help them grow their capabilities where needed.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will include a checklist and resource guide that will help ROs improve their crisis response capabilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Alex Yam would be pleased to note that.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We urge religious organisations to come on board, as we work hand in hand to ensure Singapore remains safe and united in the face of future crises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Alex Yam also asked about the international conference on Cohesive Societies.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We can learn from the experiences of others and share best practices with one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The conference will also include a track for youth leaders in the form of a young leader programme to provide the next generation of leadership a platform to tackle social challenges and find like-minded collaborators.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: By partnering youths, we benefit from their ideas and energy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They want to have the chance to shape the future, partner the Government and participate in change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this Budget, Minister Heng Swee Keat emphasised supporting our youths by improving our education system, topping-up the Edusave Account and Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA), investing in our economic sector to create more good jobs for our young people, and preparing our youths to take advantage of international business opportunities through mentorship and internship platforms.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We recognise that our youths have to navigate the ups and downs of education, work, adulthood and more.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To our youths, we hear you and understand your concerns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Since its launch last year, we have engaged over 8,000 youths from different backgrounds and stages of life, both online and face-to-face.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We listened to their interests, needs and aspirations as they spoke about various topics from mental health to environmental sustainability.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The SGYouth Action Plan will define our youths' vision for Singapore, and lay out how youths and Singapore can work together to achieve it.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Youths will have the chance to debate and discuss issues, examine policies and initiate change for the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: MCCY will be appointing a panel, comprising youth representatives, to lead this effort.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann, who will be co-leading the panel, will elaborate.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In recent years, our arts and sports scenes have flourished.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is crucial that participation in the arts and sports remains something that all Singaporeans can enjoy and benefit from.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It should not be a luxury for a privileged few.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To ensure that opportunities remain inclusive and accessible to all, we are undertaking strategic reviews of these sectors, in consultation with citizens.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, we are encouraged by the outcomes of the Arts and Culture Strategic Review (ACSR) in developing a vibrant and sustainable cultural landscape.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But we also recognise the need to update our strategies and measurements to incorporate developments since the ACSR was launched in 2012, so that our arts and culture continue to strengthen our social fabric and unity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: An important focus is to ensure our cultural offerings continue to be inclusive, particularly for underserved groups like the elderly and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The first phase of the audit will relate to infrastructure, such as general access, connectivity and wayfinding.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will also consider how we can improve the accessibility of our exhibitions and programmes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Accessibility at some of our museums and heritage institutions is already being enhanced.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The ongoing and upcoming revamps at the Changi Chapel and Museum, Reflections at Bukit Chandu, the Peranakan Museum and the Singapore Philatelic Museum will provide Singaporeans with wider passageways, lifts and ramps for wheelchair users, more nursing rooms, as well as accessible vehicle parking lots and washrooms for persons with special needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In the ongoing revamp of the Singapore Art Museum, these considerations will also be key features.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For our students, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary will share more on how we are expanding access to the arts through our schools, including School of the Arts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In Mandarin):   	Besides improving the infrastructure, we also provide new experiences and skills to seniors through a variety of activities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our heritage institutions, such as Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall, the Indian Heritage Centre and the Malay Heritage Centre, have been designated as Silver Hubs, to develop senior-friendly programmes and serve as community spaces for our elderly to come together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, we recently introduced "Reminiscence Walks", a programme that is both facilitated and attended by seniors to visit the various historical sites in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through this programme, senior volunteers can make new friends, hence, reducing the risk of social isolation.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In their golden years, seniors can enjoy an enriching life while still learning new knowledge.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They can be trained to become tour guides, allowing them to pick up new skills and benefit others as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In English): Similarly, in the sports sector, we want to ensure access and opportunities for all Singaporeans to live an active and healthy life.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Mohamad Irshad spoke about the importance of social mixing and a more inclusive society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are important community spaces where Singaporeans can meet, play and connect with one another.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will roll out accessible play spaces and facilities island-wide to bring sports closer to all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about our sports facilities and programmes going forward.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Like Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, we recognise that new and improved facilities are required to cater to the growing needs of residents and towns.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For Yishun, Sport Singapore has plans to upgrade the existing sports facilities and has engaged local community leaders on the proposed improvements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One example is the upcoming installation of LED display scoreboards and match play highlights, as well as stadium bucket seats to enhance the spectator experience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Singaporeans will also have the chance to play a bigger part in the co-creation of sporting spaces to come, such as the upgraded Choa Chu Kang Sports Centre, which will be ready in phases from 2020.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As with our cultural institutions, we are designing our sporting spaces to cater to all age groups, including our seniors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Like Ms Joan Pereira, we want our seniors to stay healthy and connected through sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Later this year, an ActiveSG gym will be opened in Ang Mo Kio CC, where seniors can participate in elder-friendly exercise programmes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Over time, we will ensure that all our ActiveSG gyms provide safe and accessible environments that are equipped for our seniors, with qualified staff onsite to provide any assistance required.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Aside from our sports infrastructure, our programmes will enable Singaporeans, young and old, to lead active lives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: ActiveSG, our national movement for sports, has gained momentum over the years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These initiatives help Singaporeans embrace an active lifestyle and connect with one another through sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, two more Academies and Clubs in Canoeing and Gymnastics will be launched, bringing our total offerings to 18, including the ActiveSG Master Club for seniors, as well as various individual and team sports for children.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I have seen and heard many positive stories of Singaporeans’ experiences in these Academies and Clubs and would like to share one example.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Earlier this year, I met nine-year-old Ethan Loh at a community event.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ethan first joined the ActiveSG Football Academy in 2016 as a beginner.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He has since gone on to represent the Academy in local and international football tournaments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Last July, he participated in the Kanga Cup in Perth, where Ethan and his team put in a strong performance, progressing to the semi-finals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I understand that Ethan also represents his school and, just yesterday, they competed in the West Zone semi-finals for the first time ever.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Beyond providing a platform for Ethan to hone his footballing skills, his father credits the Academy for helping Ethan develop into a more mature person, a testament to the holistic sporting education that ActiveSG's Academies and Clubs can provide.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To bring Active Health closer to the community, Active Health Mobile Labs were introduced last July, along with Active Health programming at the Sport-in-Precinct facilities at Jurong Spring.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are on track to open four Active Health Labs at our sport centres in Bishan, Jurong East, Sengkang and Woodlands this month, in addition to existing ones at Our Tampines Hub and Heartbeat@Bedok.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will also open two new Active Health spaces in partner facilities by May.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The first space has already been launched as part of Singapore's flagship Decathlon store in Kallang, with another to follow at Admiralty Medical Centre.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Like at the Labs, Singaporeans will be able to undergo free health and fitness assessments at these spaces and set personal health and wellness targets in consultation with sport scientists.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope to see more Singaporeans come on board Active Health in the years to come.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Next, confidence – celebrating shared values and achievements in nation-building.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is vital to our future to remember our heritage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Only by knowing where we came from, what we stand for and who we are, can we stride confidently into the future.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Prime Minister Lee announced at last year's National Day Rally that we will be nominating Hawker Culture for inscription on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Hawker Culture reflects an integral part of our way of life.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: A successful inscription will not only showcase our multicultural heritage to the world, but also our pride in our hawkers and Hawker Culture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are taking this opportunity to recognise and show appreciation to our hawkers, who reflect the trade, family spirit and rich cultural life that Singaporeans can be proud of.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will continue to engage them by featuring selected hawkers and their stories as part of the Support Our Hawkers Social Movement.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We also hope more Singaporeans will share their own hawker stories on social media with the hashtag #OurHawkerCulture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Following the initial announcement, an online poll was set up for the public to pledge their support.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Students from both Pei Chun Public School and First Toa Payoh Primary School have worked on projects related to Hawker Culture.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: One such project is Fond Memories of Toa Payoh, which saw students of both schools come together to uncover the people and stories behind hawker food in Toa Payoh, a place they proudly call a "hawker food haven".

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In addition, many private organisations and civic groups have stepped forward to support the nomination.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: You may have seen videos publicising our Hawker Culture while travelling in taxis, supported by Moove Media.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information and the National Geographic collaborated to organise the #OurHawkerCulture Photo Contest, which has seen many stunning entries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Food bloggers and influencers have been sharing stories about their favourite hawkers and hawker food and encouraging Singaporeans to do the same.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Nomination Committee, led by the National Heritage Board (NHB), the National Environment Agency and FMAS will continue to facilitate such ground-up efforts in support of our Hawker Culture, and we hope to see many more Singaporeans rallying behind this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In 2015, we started the Founders' Memorial project.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through the Founders' Memorial Committee’s engagements with the public from 2015 to 2017, Singaporeans voiced their desire for the memorial to be anchored on the values and ideals exemplified by Singapore's first generation of leaders who played important roles in Singapore's path to Independence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested a memorial for fallen soldiers at the Founders' Memorial.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Founders' Memorial, given its said purpose, would not be suited for this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We honour, in other ways, the memory of those who have given their lives for Singapore, as the Ministry of Defence mentioned in their response to a related question.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about the next phase of development for the Founders' Memorial.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The memorial will be an expression of our identity and belonging to this nation we call home.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we commemorate our history and culture, we celebrate our shared values and the success of Singaporeans on the international stage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I mentioned achievements of our Team Singapore athletes at last year's major games.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The success of our athletes is a result of years of hard work, discipline and resilience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is also an encouraging sign that our investments in the High Performance Sports (HPS) system are bearing fruit.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary will speak more about our plans for the HPS system later.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As raised by Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and earlier by Mr Terence Ho, our artists also pursue their aspirations internationally and have done Singapore proud on the world stage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will be presenting the work of multidisciplinary artist Song-Ming Ang and curator Michelle Ho, who use music to explore ideas of public involvement and the ways people relate to music, both individually and as a society.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our performing artists are flying the Singapore flag high beyond our shores.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In May, our Singapore Chinese Orchestra (SCO) will perform in South Korea, before embarking on a tour of Europe, covering Germany and Italy, later in the year.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are proud of our "people’s orchestra", whose performances will feature Singaporean artists, such as acclaimed violinist Kam Ning and percussionist Benjamin Boo.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: He holds a Bachelor of Music from the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts, and a Master of Performance from the Royal College of Music.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Benjamin joined the SCO full-time last year, following in the footsteps of his father, Mr Boo Chin Kiah, a veteran Suona musician.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They are the first father-son duo in SCO's history and will be touring together for the first time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our musicians' talent and dedication to the craft exemplify the Singapore spirit and show the world what we are capable of achieving.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We hope that showcasing our culture and heritage internationally will help people around the world learn more about Singapore.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Through volunteer.sg, volunteers can search for opportunities related to their interests and skills and share them with friends and family on social media.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Volunteers can also indicate their availability and choose preferred shifts, mark attendance and, with smart phones, track their volunteering hours, and provide feedback to organisers with ease.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For our volunteer managers, this integrated system provides a digital solution for better management of volunteering opportunities and engagement of volunteers, thus enabling them to scale up.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we bring more agencies on board the platform to provide a wider range of volunteering opportunities, we hope to see even more Singaporeans come forward and contribute to our culture of care.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Technology can also be an effective tool for engagement and dialogue.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Later this year, we will be launching an online site so that youths can participate in conversations with one another and engage with the Government on issues close to their hearts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This digital deliberation platform will complement the live Youth Conversations, and the Senior Minister of State will elaborate further.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During the Budget Debate, Mr Terence Ho gave a thoughtful speech on the application of technology in arts and culture to meet the changing needs and preferences of audiences.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This year, we will roll out the first phase of our plan to digitalise the culture sector, to engage new audiences and make it easier for all Singaporeans to enjoy arts and culture as part of daily life.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our initiative under this plan is a Cultural Concierge, a one-stop online platform to discover arts and culture activities and content.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Users will be able to search for event listings according to individual preferences, using key words, such as "nearby", "weekend" or "family-friendly", as well as interact with a chatbot for event and content recommendations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The website will also be integrated with relevant ticketing sites, for a seamless user experience.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will also launch the Cultural Resource Ontology, to enhance online search capabilities for both the public and researchers to access cultural resources more easily.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will leverage technology to enhance visitor experiences and improve operations at our cultural and sporting spaces.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NHB launched the DigiMuse programme last August, and will be holding another edition this year to trial new technology, such as Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, chatbots and assistive technology in its galleries.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the sporting front, we are implementing the Computer Vision Drowning Detection System at our public swimming complexes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Using a network of overhead infrared cameras, the system enables earlier detection of possible drowning, thus making our pools safer.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Mr Chairman, we are living in times where the only constant is change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Change can be unsettling and may leave some people behind.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We need to ride the wave of change together.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At MCCY, we will continue to foster a culture of care and trust.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will ensure that everyone has the opportunity to contribute to society and pursue their dreams.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Every Singaporean has a part to play, from volunteering, leading ground-up projects, contributing to a cause, empowering our youths, to supporting our artists and athletes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And it is not just in MCCY's domain that Singaporeans can contribute.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And we have seen many impactful Government-citizen partnerships in different sectors, and we look forward to many more meaningful engagements and collaborations in the years to come.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Together, we can inspire confidence that Singapore will continue to succeed and be a place we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, our Bicentennial is an excellent opportunity for us to reflect on what makes Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The spirit of sharing and helping others, as encapsulated by the SG Cares movement that started in end 2016 is really one of the oldest strands in our DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many of our forefathers arrived on this island hungry, tired, but hopeful; often bringing not much more with them than the clothes on their back, their energy and their pluck.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With few of their needs provided for in a fledgling port colony, they learned quickly to self-organise and support one another.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Although wealthy philanthropists did emerge, much of the help that our forefathers gave to one another was modest and informal, made all the more meaningful because the givers often did not have much themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, we gave names to this sense of fellow-feeling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We called it "gotong royong", or the "kampong spirit".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Other strands, equally old, also exist in our DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Almost all trades and professions that our forefathers engaged in depended directly or indirectly on our free-trading port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Livelihoods and fortunes were tied to the world's inclination to buy and sell, and the laws of demand and supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such an environment favoured the qualities of ruggedness, self-reliance and a pragmatic focus on material well-being. "Gotong royong" and self-reliance sound like opposites but are long-standing and complementary elements of what make Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They pre-date the emergence of independent nationhood and also pre-date taxes and transfers as a way of redistributing wealth from those who have more to those with less.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Indeed, as Members of this House know, help for vulnerable members of our society is delivered in no small part through the mechanism of taxes and transfers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We actively debate the merits of these schemes in this House, and will no doubt continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But relying on taxes and transfers alone to deliver help is not enough.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is not enough to create the social bonds that arise from assistance voluntarily given and warmly received.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And many intangible goods that make such a positive difference to our lives do not come in the form of subsidies, vouchers and rebates – intangible goods like companionship, shared experience and individual autonomy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why we should not forget how we came to value both "gotong royong" and the spirit of self-reliance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Several Members have spoken on the importance of volunteerism, including Ms Irene Quay and Mr Yee Chia Hsing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: My Ministry's approach is to get more people involved in volunteering; to drive volunteerism within our other domain areas like the arts, sports and heritage; and to support the giving sector through capacity-building and funding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Promoting corporate and senior volunteerism are two key strategies in our efforts to get more people involved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our findings have shown that volunteerism rates dip at two life stages – when youths transit from school to work, and when people approach retirement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will focus our efforts on connecting more young working adults and seniors with volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that many young adults devote much of their time at work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The workplace is thus a natural touchpoint to reconnect with those who have volunteered as students and reach those who have yet to experience volunteering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We want to encourage more to start, and to help those which already do to expand their efforts and reach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree with Mr Yee Chia Hsing that it is important to ensure that CSR efforts are beneficial to both the giver and recipient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Companies that lack the knowledge and expertise to develop meaningful initiatives can tap on informational resources available under the Company of Good programme created by NVPC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Starting later this year, NVPC will serve as the first port of call for companies embarking on CSR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Companies can approach NVPC directly to be referred to volunteering opportunities that meet their interests and requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NVPC will closely partner key agencies like the National Council of Social Service in this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To encourage more corporates along their volunteering journey, we will simplify the claims process of the existing BIPS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also engage companies and IPCs more proactively on BIPS through NVPC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As Singapore's largest employer, the Public Service will set a good example and take the lead by rallying officers to volunteer under the Public Service Cares (PS Cares) movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY will partner the Public Service Division and support Government agencies' CSR representatives to develop more varied and impactful giving opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While working in the Ministry of Home Affairs' headquarters as a former policy officer, I was introduced to my first volunteering opportunities by my Home Team colleagues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They encouraged me to tutor girls from troubled backgrounds living in a residential facility and, later, inmates studying for the GCE "A" level in the Prison School.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will always remain grateful for these opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Without these first steps, I would not have discovered my own interest in ground work nor have gone on to seek out more volunteering opportunities in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Volunteering also gave me a better appreciation of the wide range of issues and challenges faced by my public sector colleagues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Within the domain of any one public sector agency, there are already good opportunities for its staff to give.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With a strong PS Cares movement, these opportunities will multiply, and more good matches can be made between a wider range of needs, and a wider range of skillsets and interests among givers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Not only can more public officers derive personal satisfaction from helping others, but they can also gain new insights into domains of public service that they might not otherwise be exposed to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can encourage officers to do more and engender greater impact from the ground-up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Kwok Jia Chuan from the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office, for example, co-founded Conjunct Consulting (Conjunct) in 2011.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Conjunct is a non-profit social change organisation borne out of Jia Chuan's goal of strengthening the capabilities of the social service sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the past seven years, Jia Chuan has helped create sustainable strategies for many organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He also encouraged other professionals and civil servants to mentor and guide student volunteers in Conjunct projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A growing number of our seniors are educated, skilled, socially active and keen to contribute impactfully to our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many of them are among the Merdeka Generation, and some are even Pioneers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We want to welcome more of them into the ranks of volunteers as volunteering is one of the most rewarding ways to age actively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY is working with community partners, such as the Organisation of Senior Volunteers (RSVP) Singapore and the Centre for Seniors, to engage seniors at their workplaces and raise pre-retirement awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To begin, roadshows and lunchtime talks will be held to highlight the many ways in which seniors can volunteer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, "Retire with a Purpose" by RSVP Singapore is one programme that introduces employees 40 and above to volunteering opportunities, equips them with relevant skills, and plugs them into an active and like-minded community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Another platform for seniors to consider is the Mentoring Alliance, a recent ground-up initiative by 11 youth and social service organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is an ambitious but not impossible goal, because I believe there are many untapped potential mentors out there, especially among our older Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Those who are prepared to offer their wisdom and life experiences can make extraordinary impact in shaping the lives of young Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also agree with Ms Irene Quay that it is important to tap on the skills and expertise of business and public sector leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Centre for Non-Profit Leadership's Board Match Programme reaches out to professionals across industries to identify candidates who can serve non-profit organisations (NPOs) in a leadership capacity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Candidates are matched to various leadership roles depending on their skills and seniority, according to the needs of the organisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such matching enables retiring or retired business and public leaders to contribute impactfully, while NPOs benefit from their expertise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY will continue to develop volunteerism in the other domain areas we oversee – the arts, heritage and sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the arts, we will sustain current efforts to promote arts access to under-reached communities through ArtReach initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our Befrienders Arts Toolkit, created by local artists, has enabled volunteers and staff at care centres to befriend more effectively by introducing hands-on arts activities and new conversation topics with beneficiaries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since its rollout last year, 1,200 kits have been distributed to 11 social service organisations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since HeritageCares began in 2016, over 3,200 volunteers, including corporates and youths, have been engaged as befrienders or guides for various NHB programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our volunteers go the extra mile to make our museums and heritage institutions inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, for example, HeritageCares partnered the Movement for the Intellectually Disabled Singapore and the Cerebral Palsy Alliance (Singapore) School to organise training sessions for volunteers and museum docents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This helps our volunteers provide quality experiences for visitors of all abilities to our museums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In sports, we seek more sporting opportunities for vulnerable and underserved communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportCares will develop Communities of Care, an initiative aimed at addressing the needs of the vulnerable and underserved, such as youths-at-risk and isolated seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This initiative marks SportCares' shift in focus toward network-building and scaling up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, SportSG will partner Glyph, a social service organisation, to organise weekly SportCares swimming sessions for children from lower-income families to build up their resilience and confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More details will be shared in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, Team Nila comprises a diverse group of 20,000 volunteers spanning all backgrounds, races and ages, united by their passion to give back through sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have proven themselves to be a vibrant and energetic volunteer force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We can do more to tap on Team Nila's enthusiasm, skills and networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SportSG is helping volunteers to step up and assume larger leadership and organisational roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, we have put in place various grants and funds to grow our climate of giving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These funds served to encourage contributions by donors, and are an added push to level up sectoral capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, these matching funds are tailored to meet each sector's specific needs and challenges, and promote shared ownership by deepening partnerships within the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Over the years, we have put in place various grants and funds to grow our climate of giving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These funds serve to encourage contributions by donors and to level up sectoral capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In addition, these matching funds are tailored to meet each sector's specific needs and challenges, and promote shared ownership by deepening partnerships within the community.
