speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, the Cultural Matching Fund seeks to promote cultural philanthropy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also have the One Team Singapore Fund in support of Team Singapore Athletes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Fund is meant to encourage a spirit of giving in our bicentennial year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: BCF is a one-off boost to our local giving ecosystem, channelled through our IPCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our IPCs are held to a higher standard of regulatory compliance and governance by the Commissioner of Charities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As more donors start the habit of giving, we expect a ripple effect in the wider giving ecosystem, which includes non-government organisations and ground-up groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are mindful that some charities, especially the smaller ones, may face resource constraints in their governance efforts and in meeting regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To help them, the Commissioner of Charities will streamline and simplify regulatory reporting requirements, particularly for smaller charities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Clearer guidance to charities will be provided via the Charity Portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will also expand various outreach initiatives, such as shared services and training sessions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Commissioner of Charities has plans to increase the number of shared services to help smaller charities be more cost-effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This year, charities will also have access to a wider range of learning opportunities to develop their capabilities for good governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For instance, we are jointly collaborating with the Singapore Institute of Directors and the Charity Council to kickstart our inaugural series of "In Conversation with the Commissioner of Charities" in April, with the first session focusing on Board Culture, Ethics and Governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Chairman, I had begun my speech by referring to "gotong royong" as a very old strand in Singapore's DNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the Bicentennial commemoration, we will have opportunities to examine and appreciate many other elements that make Singaporeans who we are and reflect on our past, present and future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked how our nation’s shared values will be brought out through the Bicentennial programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our values of openness, multiculturalism and self-determination are reflected, first and foremost, in the enthusiasm of community groups to take the lead in commemoration activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More than half of the nearly 180 Bicentennial-related events are community-led or initiated, and MCCY is supporting more than 30 of such efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One of these ground-up projects is "Forge of Nations", a family card game developed by Mr Wan Jun Yan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As village chiefs in 20th century Southeast Asia, players have to make decisions on their population and infrastructure to transform into a nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The game allows an appreciation of the challenges our predecessors faced and the values that have shaped Singapore over the past 200 years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our multicultural heritage will also be commemorated through the Bicentennial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singaporeans can look forward to the Eurasian Festival in July supported by Our Singapore Fund, as well as special upcoming exhibitions on the lives and contributions of our early migrants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These exhibitions will be featured in the Malay and Indian Heritage Centres and the Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As we look back at our past and examine the present during our bicentennial year, it is also timely to look ahead and ask, "What next?" The exercise of charting our future would be incomplete without engaging our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Henry Kwek and Mr Darryl David asked for an update on the Youth Conversations as well as MCCY's plans to give youths a bigger voice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The younger generation in any given era can always be expected to think, behave and communicate somewhat differently from those who are older.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, the rise of digital technology and social media has now accelerated changes in how youths produce and consume goods, services and information; relate to one another; and derive meaning and identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This has created more diversity in our midst but also the potential for significant divergence in values and choices between generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We need to understand these shifts in the youth sector well and to respond to them meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They spoke candidly and eloquently on their aspirations and hopes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Many care deeply about their relationships with their parents and families and want to make them proud and happy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also care about achieving personal success on their own terms in the eyes of their peers and society at large, and wonder whether they can do so, all at the same time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They sometimes worry about whether there are gaps between what they love to do and what others want for them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They also have a keen desire to help shape a future Singapore that is even better than today by opening up more pathways to success, doing more for the environment and becoming a more inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are interested in understanding more, too, about the viewpoints, preferences and choices of those who are older than them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In attending Youth Conversations, I encountered some views I had anticipated and some that I had not, all of which were intriguing and rewarding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More insights from Youth Conversations will be available in an interim report to be released later this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Youth Conversations have given us a good sense of our youths’ aspirations, needs and interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We know the youths want to move these conversations into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will be co-leading a Panel comprising youth leaders from various sectors and organisations to develop this Action Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Panel will work closely with Government agencies and the National Youth Council to engage youths from all walks of life and other stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From the Youth Conversations, we know that such issues could range from jobs and employment to mental well-being and environmental sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These engagements will be carried out both online and face-to-face, and details will be announced later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Panel will also identify opportunities for youths to provide recommendations on policies and create partnership projects with the Government, communities, non-profits and businesses to spearhead the change they hope to see.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Seeds of change are being planted even now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SOAR aims to combat the social stigma associated with mental health issues through community workshops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Other youths from the same Youth Conversation have also stepped up, with some forming a panel of resource persons for the Health Promotion Board (HPB).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They have provided feedback for HPB's programmes and collaterals, shared insights into mental health-related issues among young people and raised awareness of HPB’s initiatives in their own networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Within the Action Plan, youths can also get involved in the transformation of the Youth Belt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As part of the larger Orchard Road rejuvenation plan, we want to develop a vibrant youth district at Somerset that supports our youths’ aspirations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Spaces along Somerset Road, such as *SCAPE, The Red Box and Skate Park, have already been serving as congregation points for youths, featuring music and media, entrepreneurship, learning and urban sports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But as Orchard Road renews itself, we have a unique opportunity to re-imagine the Youth Belt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We will be engaging youths through a placemaking exercise, with online and face-to-face sessions, so that they can show us how to take this youth precinct to the next level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Youth Belt is but one of the many partnerships we hope to engender under the Youth Action Plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us give our youths a headstart in leading the way into the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us help them get going on the next chapter of the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Our shared values, as embedded in our DNA, will be an important guiding light as we chart the future of our Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Sim Ann)
text: MCCY will continue to actively partner the community in building a caring and inclusive home together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the arts, heritage and sports are integral to making Singapore a vibrant and liveable city, and for Singaporeans to lead well-rounded and fulfilling lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They can inspire us, affirm our shared values and make us proud of what we stand for.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They provide opportunities for Singaporeans of all backgrounds to showcase their talents, pursue their dreams and come together to create shared memories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our SG Arts Plan, Our SG Heritage Plan, and Vision 2030 are roadmaps that provide multi-year directions and guide the development of our sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will talk about some key focus areas for this year, beginning with the arts and heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Henry Kwek asked about our Arts and Culture Strategic Review (ACSR).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the same period, our arts and heritage activities have seen increases in number, variety and attendance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, we recognise that our strategies and approaches must be updated to address new developments that have taken place since then.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These are reflected in Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans, introduced in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They were done in consultation with about 1,500 stakeholders across the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our SG Arts Plan comprises three strategic thrusts of (a) inspiring our people, (b) connecting our communities and (c) positioning Singapore globally.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I will touch on the key initiatives that will support each thrust.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To inspire audiences, our artists must be able to produce high-quality and impactful work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will provide capability development platforms for our artists across various artforms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Writers in English, Chinese, Malay and Tamil will benefit from masterclasses by international, regional and local talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our writers will also benefit from peer-learning and opportunities to build communities across cultures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To support our artists, we will continue the Community Arts Residency programme, just piloted last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It aims to reflect the collective stories of our people by providing artists with spaces in the community to develop arts collaborations with residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over four months in 2018, the residency supported visual artist Terence Lin, who organised house visits, invited residents to his open house, and facilitated artmaking sessions with seniors and youths living in and around Taman Jurong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The project culminated in an exhibition of residents’ artworks, items and audio interviews at the Taman Jurong CC.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is also important that we help arts practitioners, including our arts freelancers, build sustainable careers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC consulted over 370 members of our arts community last year to understand the specific needs of freelancers that will enable them to be more self-sufficient and financially independent, not just during their working life, but prepare them for retirement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To address some of the findings, NAC will establish freelance resource hubs and work with partners to offer shared resources and services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These include insurance coverage, connecting freelancers with relevant service providers, and making available jobs, contracts and projects as well as a database of talents and expertise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, we would like freelancers to benefit from national schemes, such as SkillsFuture, to enhance their employability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Earlier, the Ministry of Manpower announced that the Government, as a service buyer, will pilot the Contribute-as-You-Earn (CAYE) model early next year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will allow for smaller but regular contributions to MediSave, instead of bigger lumpsums at year-end.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MCCY, NAC and NHB are looking forward to participating in this pilot, so that our freelancers can better save for their healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Some people may think that artists create works based on a single moment of inspiration but, in reality, many artworks are based on a deep understanding of the subject matter, presented from a well thought through perspective.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Therefore, NAC will strengthen research support in the arts so that artists can further grow their practice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Research can also help arts groups better understand and develop their audiences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, we want to better understand the long-term value and impact of arts engagement on different population segments.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will support more research studies in these areas and publish a monthly e-newsletter to share relevant research with the arts community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is also organising a research symposium next week that brings academics and artists together to discuss the impact of the arts on space, people and communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The second thrust of Our SG Arts Plan seeks to connect diverse groups with the arts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One key group is our youths, who are important as arts enthusiasts and practitioners not only of today but for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC, the National Youth Council (NYC) and *SCAPE will create more platforms for our youths to develop and showcase their talents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, diverse music acts from NAC's Noise Singapore performed at NYC’s YOUTHx, thereby reinforcing our youths’ interests and aspirations in music.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will elevate the profile of our young artists and help them grow a larger audience base.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC will also work with *SCAPE under its Arts and Culture Nodes network.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our existing nodes enrich and enliven neighbourhoods around Singapore through regular and accessible arts programmes. *SCAPE will be our next node and will showcase more art that resonates with young people and give our youths more chances to exhibit their works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the wider public, our signature showcases, such as the Singapore International Festival of Arts, Singapore Writers Festival, and Singapore Biennale, bring art closer to the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, the 7th edition of the Singapore Art Week in January showcased over 100 diverse programmes in venues, such as the Singapore Art Museum, Gillman Barracks, Little India and Sim Lim Square.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Terence Ho spoke about the importance of promoting Singapore’s cultural talents overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are proud of our arts practitioners who venture overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This not only helps artists hone their skills and develop new markets but also showcases Singapore’s culture internationally and promotes people-to-people links.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to facilitate such efforts by building our overseas networks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, our cultural institutions participate in platforms, such as the International Committee for Museums and Collections of Modern Art, Association of Asia Pacific Performing Arts, and the International Society for the Performing Arts (ISPA).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, we will emphasise the development of visual arts residencies in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, under NAC’s partnership with the Cemeti Institute for Art and Society, we will begin sending Singaporean artists for residencies in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, starting from September.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NAC is also exploring similar opportunities in the Philippines and Thailand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With a deeper understanding of this vibrant region’s shared heritage and future, our artists will be well-placed to produce even more compelling works.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also support our performing artists in countries, such as Australia, China, Japan, the UK and France.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An example is Shaza Ishak, Teater Ekamatra’s General Manager and Company Director, who was funded by NAC to represent Singapore at the prestigious ISPA Fellowship Programme from 2017 to 2019, and the Australian Performing Arts Market in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Arising from this, Teater Ekamatra, DramaBox and Australia's PVI collective are now developing TOPIA – an international residency exchange programme in Singapore and Perth.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now speak in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):  	We will help our writers secure developmental opportunities overseas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will help our homegrown talents to hone their skills and take Singapore's literary offerings abroad.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lu Xun Academy of Literature is a top-rated academy based in Beijing which hosted notable Chinese writers, such as Wang Anyi and the winner of 2012 Nobel Prize in Literature, Mo Yan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through this residency programme, our artists will have the opportunities to learn from best practices and advance in their craft.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In English) Let me now move on to our shared heritage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since the launch of Our SG Heritage Plan in 2018, we have made progress across its four pillars: Our Places, Our Cultures, Our Treasures, Our Communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our tangible heritage remains important markers of the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NHB's 18 heritage trails help us to document and increase awareness of the heritage of the places where we live, work and play.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Last year, NHB launched the Orchard Heritage Trail and refreshed the Bukit Timah Heritage Trail.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2019, NHB and HDB will be launching the Pasir Ris Heritage Trail as part of HDB’s “Remaking Our Heartland” programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The public can look out for an open call for community contributions of stories.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To promote awareness and appreciation of our 72 National Monuments, NHB will introduce a new annual programme "Milestones through Monuments".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It will highlight the roles of these monuments during significant episodes in our history and encourage the public to have meaningful experiences at our historic sites.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The inaugural edition will be held in late 2019 and will feature a race with stops at our National Monuments along the Singapore River.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: NHB will also continue working with MOE to enhance the various education programmes at our museums.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, pilots of the Museum Educators Programme were conducted at the Asian Civilisations Museum and National Museum of Singapore last year, which included the engagement of 20 retired educators and museum docents to support interactive learning experiences for over 2,100 primary and secondary school students from nine schools.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are reviewing the pilots and refining the programme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The content presented in both experiences will reinforce learning points about our history and the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Minister and Senior Minister of State spoke about reaching underserved communities through our Heritage Institutions and programmes like HeritageCares.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will also be leveraging technology to transform the way we engage.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Beyond our museums and heritage institutions, we also recognise the importance of community-led events in celebrating and safeguarding our heritage and traditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing spoke on the success of the recent River Hongbao, an event organised by the Chinese community since 1987.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have supported the event as part of the Chinese New Year celebrations, as well as the Hari Raya and Deepavali light-ups in past years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year’s River Hongbao was a successful commemoration of our Bicentennial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Kudos to the Organising Chair Mr Ang Wei Neng and his team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are heartened that community support for these cultural events has been strong and hope that such support will continue to grow.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan and Mr Henry Kwek asked for an update on V2030.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In the past seven years, recommendations had been progressively implemented in the form of ActiveSG, Team Nila, our Disability Sports Master Plan, and the HPS system, just to name a few.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will share the updated V2030 recommendations later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: A major part of V2030 is about bringing Singaporeans from all walks of life together through sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2016, we launched the Disability Sports Master Plan, which has, to date, seen the opening of five Inclusive Gyms by ActiveSG.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Our annual Inclusive Sports Festival also saw a doubling in participants with disabilities last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This year, SportSG will expand Play Inclusive, Singapore’s largest unified sports competition, which is organised by Special Olympics Singapore and supported by MOE's Special Education Branch.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The two-day event will pair athletes from special education schools and adult disability centres with students from neighbouring mainstream schools to form more inclusive teams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Altogether, SportSG's programmes have introduced sports ranging from swimming to wheelchair rugby to over 500 persons with disabilities over the last three years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Leonard Lu, a wheelchair user, is one of our programme participants who is now leading a much more active lifestyle, after joining the Yes!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: He now makes weekly visits to the inclusive gym, accompanied by his mother, Natalie.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: He has built up strength and is walking more during his exercise sessions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Leonard gets stronger, he is enjoying more sports activities, such as canoeing and kayaking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SportSG will continue its outreach efforts to raise awareness in the community and develop organisational and professional capabilities in disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Currently, plans are underway to build the capabilities of teachers and staff at special education schools and disability centres in conducting sporting activities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They will work with sport coaches to co-create and tailor sport activities that meet the needs of their students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Yip Pin Xiu asked if we can make sports more inclusive in Singapore by integrating our NSAs to oversee able-bodied and disability sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This has to be decided by the sports fraternities themselves and their NSAs, which are non-government organisations that operate firmly on the principle of independence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The International Olympic Committee and the International Paralympic Committee oversee the various National Olympic and Paralympic Committees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These include the Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC) and the Singapore National Paralympic Council (SNPC) which, in turn, oversee the development and promotion of the Olympic and Paralympic Movements in Singapore, as well as the selection of Team Singapore athletes for the major games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The NSAs not only have to align with the SNOC and SNPC, but also their respective International Sports Federations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They take reference from their parent bodies in how they organise themselves, and are also accountable to them for the development of the sport in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In this regard, the NSAs play an important role in leading their fraternities in the development and promotion of their sports as well as supporting the high-performance development of their national athletes through coaching and competition opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While respecting that NSAs are independent organisations, SportSG partners them to develop their sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, SportSG provides eligible NSAs facilities, funding and technical support to implement their Multi-Year Sports Plans, which address the development of top athletes and grow the sport’s participation base.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It also works with NSAs to strengthen their organisational capabilities and governance standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In addition, SportSG provides all Singaporeans with opportunities to develop their sporting potential through programmes, such as ActiveSG Academies and Clubs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One encouraging example is Mr Tan Whee Boon, who lost part of his limbs to an unfortunate bacterial infection in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like Leonard Lu, he started at our Yes!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I Can Swim programme in 2016 when we launched the first Centre of Expertise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, 2016, three years ago, was already very different from Ms Yip Pin Xiu's experience in the 1990s.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For Wee Boon, he has since gone on to try out a lot of different sports, including scuba diving under our SportCares programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through such opportunities and exposure, Whee Boon discovered his passion and talent for rugby and has since gone on to pursue competitive rugby as a part of Singapore's first wheelchair rugby team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: When it comes to disability sports, some International Sports Federations integrate the development of able-bodied athletes and those with disabilities, whilst others prefer to do it separately.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In Singapore, the NSAs for Cycling, Equestrian and Sailing oversee the development of athletes of all abilities, with Table Tennis set to join their ranks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We would want to see more NSAs adopt an inclusive approach in developing our national athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We aim to achieve what is best for all athletes, regardless of ability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While integrating able-bodied and para sports in a single NSA has its benefits, we understand there might be concerns from the disability sports fraternity that doing so may dilute attention on para sports.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For sports that are exclusive to athletes with disabilities, such as goalball, SportSG will continue to support the work of the Singapore Disability Sports Council, which partners the respective National Disability Sports Associations to realise synergies in outreach and public education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Whether in able-bodied or disability sports, whether they are integrated in the same NSA or not, MCCY will continue to support our Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Their successes, amidst each achievement, provide Singaporeans occasions to come together as one nation and ignite our sense of optimism and "can-do" spirit, and this is what Mr Lee Yi Shyan has also spoken about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For many national athletes, the road to success has multiple entry points and pathways.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is crucial that we have a strong sports ecosystem to support them at every stage of their journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Darryl David and Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked about Team Singapore's preparations for upcoming major games, the 30th SEA Games and 10th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Para Games this year in the Philippines, and the 32nd Olympic Games and 16th Paralympic Games in Japan next year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We continue to work with key stakeholders to ensure that our HPS system nurtures our athletes to greater heights and maximises their potential.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is something which Mr Lee Yi Shyan also raised, and I agree that more can be done to help our national athletes achieve their best.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Athletes also enjoy a higher quantum of spexGrants, such as spex Training Assistance Grant (spexTAG), which help defray training equipment and other costs incurred by our national athletes, and the Sports Excellence Grant for Loss of Wages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As part of his preparations, he is receiving additional funding to defray his full-time training expenses, including equipment costs, as well as his participation in more overseas competitions and training stints.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that the enhanced campaign support will benefit Ahmad's long-term high performance sports development, which will put him in good stead for the upcoming SEA Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing also asked how we are developing our HPS ecosystem to meet the challenges of the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are committed to supporting our athletes' personal development, helping them balance the demands of high performance sports with education goals, and preparing them for a smooth transition to a post-sport career.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Under the spexBusiness Network, SSI works with corporate partners to offer professional development opportunities with flexible work arrangements, as well as mentorship on starting a business.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since 2013, the network has grown from seven to 61 companies, benefiting over 230 Team Singapore athletes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One example is Chelsea Ann Sim, a three-time SEA Games medallist in taekwondo.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through the spexBusiness Network, OSIM and Deloitte offered her internships in 2016 and 2018, respectively.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Such opportunities enabled Chelsea to gain work experience while juggling her sporting goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Chelsea graduated from the Singapore Management University last year and is now working full time with Deloitte as a Clients and Markets Executive, while concurrently training for the upcoming SEA Games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about the developments in local football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Football is a sport with mass appeal and potential to bring Singaporeans from different backgrounds together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like many Singaporeans, we would like to see improvement in the standard of Singapore football and the performance of our national teams.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have seen some improvements in the past year, such as a stronger focus on player fitness, resulting in higher standards of play.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The exposure given to U-23 players will also strengthen our major games squads and provide a stronger foundation to build the national team.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: SportSG has been progressively upgrading these stadia to improve spectator experience at football matches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Fans can look forward to LED scoreboards, electronic A-boards, improved sound systems, and stronger club branding at these venues, while the SPL teams can look forward to better changing room facilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Singapore Sports School is also doing its part to develop a pool of young talents, by following the FAS coaching syllabus for its football academy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Student-footballers are also provided with overseas exposure through competitions and training exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One example is national footballer, Adam Swandi, who went to Japan for training stints during his time in the Sports School.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This contributed to his long-term development as a professional footballer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2018, Adam, who was previously with Albirex Niigata Singapore Football Club (FC), played a key role in his team's SPL title win.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: He has since transferred to Home United FC in January to further his sporting career.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For the wider community, SportSG's ActiveSG Football Academy partners FAS to develop structured programmes to provide opportunities for more young Singaporeans to develop football skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We hope that this will encourage and sustain mass participation in football, build a wider talent pool, and foster a stronger football culture.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The FAS leadership will also continue to and has to engage the clubs, stakeholders and fans, and work closely with them on this journey to improve the state of Singapore football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In response to Mr Faisal Manap's point, all our Team Singapore athletes have coped with and have strived within Singapore's unique ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is not easy, but many of them have been able to balance their sporting pursuits with commitments, whether it is National Service, education or career and they have done well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We wish FAS all the best and we will continue to support FAS and our national team to raise the standard of Singapore football.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, building a strong nation requires us to recognise the diverse talents, gifts and dreams of each individual, and to support one another to be our best selves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Together, we can celebrate our collective achievements and be confident in our future.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, I have a clarification for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the NAC look at contracts that have been given out to arts freelancers by, say, production houses, venue owners, recipients of NAC fund, to ensure that the contracts comply with the tripartite standards that all Government procurement entities have already adopted, so that the contracts are fair and that freelancers who sign on to the contracts get their fair deal and reasonable terms in those contracts?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And a second clarification will be that I am glad that the Ministry is offering an online resource for arts freelancers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: When will NAC consider a shared workplace for arts freelancers to come together to work, to exchange ideas and to interact?

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Chairman, I asked a Parliamentary Question last month regarding pool safety for private pools.

speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching
text: Can I ask Minister Grace Fu if there are intentions to extend the drowning detectors to private pools and make it mandatory because this is more urgent as the private pools actually do not have lifeguards onsite?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Chairman, I would like to thank Ms Irene Quay for her suggestion.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And as Members can see, the implementation is quite phased out because we are still testing the technology and want to make sure that it gives us good value before we decide on broad-based implementation.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I heard the Senior Parliamentary Secretary saying that the national team's coach will be announced in June.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: According to a media report on 25 February, the FAS President mentioned that the selection process is already at the tail-end.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I was referring to today's media report about what FAS has said – that they are at the tail-end and are looking towards appointing the national coach in time for the competition in June.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I think by June, they will appoint the national coach.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a selection process by FAS itself.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I do not know exactly what caused the duration of time for the process.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But I believe the selection of the national coach is a very important part of the development of high performance in football.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I believe the FAS leadership must have taken a hard look at evaluating the choices for the national coach.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, could I ask Senior Minister of State Sim Ann this: there have been a lot of Government-driven efforts in community-building and there are also a lot of ground-up initiatives.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How can we deepen these communities by encouraging both of these communities to come together to collaborate so that we do not actually build siloed communities as an unintended consequence?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I think what Ms Anthea Ong asked is at the heart of many of the efforts that we are doing in MCCY across all domains.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The key I think is in coordination in outreach and networking.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The approach taken under the SG Cares umbrella is, first and foremost, bringing stakeholders together, for instance, the service providers, experts who have been studying various social issues, as well as champions for beneficiaries who understand particular aspects of their needs and aspirations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And we have found in instances where this occurs, that the networking and information sharing very often lead to new ways of collaborating, new partnerships, and I think all these will only serve to further benefit the vulnerable segments in society and, in the process, make many of these voluntary organisations stronger because they learn from one another.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For spexScholarships, it consists of the allowance for the athletes, and it also has the support of overseas training tournaments and so on.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: In the event that the athletes do not take up the spexScholarship, will this overseas training assistance be given to the NSA?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: In short, will the NSAs be worse off if their athletes decide not to take up the spexScholarship?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For someone to take up the spexScholarship, there is a commitment to train full-time.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Besides this, NSAs also put in place multi-year plans, which the NSAs can discuss with SportSG.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This includes support for the training and development needs of athletes, including athletes who turned down spexScholarship.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Because the timeframe for both the spexScholarship and the multi-year sports plan is synced, NSAs would have a good picture of what is coming up and, therefore, will be able to put together the resources.

speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu
text: So, can there be more funding towards SDSC?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Her story is an inspiration for all of us.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As for funding for SDSC, it is part of SportSG's overall plan to support all NSAs.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Depending on the plan, the strategy is to develop that sport or many sports in SDSC.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, the achievements of Team Singapore athletes, and also efforts promoting mass participation, will all be taken into consideration.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We note that SDSC's plate is very full with different sports, and we will give them our best support to help our athletes achieve their dreams.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, building on the point that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary made earlier on the spexScholarship, there is still a difference in the level of funding between the multi-year programme as well as the spexScholarship.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Perhaps, one suggestion would be to make the spexScholarship a little bit flexible because they have different elements to the spexScholarship.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: In certain cases, the athlete does not take up the scholarship because their current income is already higher than what the spexScholarship would provide.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When we first came up with the spexScholarship, it was really to support athletes who want to train full-time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In other words, the athlete who declares, "I want to dedicate my time, maybe next two, three, four years, to competitive sport and I really want to have the support to do that." That was the genesis of spexScholarship.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is not just money, it is a commitment about dedicating your time and energy.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There is also underlying it a sort of an undertaking that you will do well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There are certain targets that we will set out, together with the athletes, coaches and the NSAs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If someone has a well-paying job, then, actually, the question is: where do sports stand in relation to the career?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, whether he will still be able to meet the kind of expectation under a spexScholarship, that is something we need to discuss with the athletes and also with the NSAs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is important for us to see that in perspective.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Definitely, if the athlete is already well-supported, does not need to have the income to train, I do not think we need to put a scholarship in front of the person.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We can use the money for other purposes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If that athlete is also joining the team in overseas training and so on, it will be considered as part of the funding grant.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Chairman, I would like to ask the Ministry regarding BCF.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I understand, in terms of implementation and governance, that we focus on the IPCs.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The Senior Minister of State said that there are about 600 IPCs in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: But we also know that there are many, many more registered charities that are not IPCs, the smaller organisations as well as the ground-ups and social enterprises, that, in my view, should also be enfolded into this Bicentennial commemoration and to support them.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share what else we can do to support these other organisations that are not IPCs, because it clearly disadvantages them?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Because any time there is a matching grant – when I was President of Women's Initiative for Ageing Successfully – for SG50 Care and Share, a lot of funds do go to the IPCs, away from the other non-IPCs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Chairman, I want to assure Ms Anthea Ong that there are many other sources of funding in support of all groups, regardless of whether they are IPCs.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It includes our network as well as capability-building platforms that are run by NVPC.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also hope that more of them can do that, so that they can be more transparent and accountable to donors, and that helps them reach out to an even larger pool of givers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: That is actually the reason why there is a distinction in treatment between organisations that have attained IPC and those that have not.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, for those who have yet to do so, there is support for them to get there, because it is ultimately towards the very laudable goals of better governance.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Sorry, Mr Chairman, I forgot to declare earlier my interest as the Deputy President of STTA.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: We receive funding from MCCY as well as having a number of spexScholars on our list.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: To clarify the point I made earlier, some of the athletes that I referred to are already full-time athletes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: They are receiving their income through the NSA.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As I have explained earlier, there are various ways that SportSG can support NSAs in the development of athletes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, perhaps the Member can take this outside of the Chamber to discuss how we could support STTA more.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, I just want to support Ms Yip Pin Xiu's re-imagining inclusive sports.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I just want to ask if MCCY funds SportSG which funds the NSAs, then why can MCCY not request these agencies to be more inclusive in their visioning?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We do not have to do everything now, but maybe re-imagine, and I am sure we would like them to be independent.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But, surely, as funders, you can strongly suggest that they can re-imagine a bit of the vision.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would just like to share my perspective on this.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In my earlier years in MOE, I had the privilege of making some work visits to Australia to study the special needs education sector.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In one of those visits, we were in a suburban area, and they showed us a school which was supposed to be very inclusive.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It takes in any child that basically requests to be in that school.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I was very attracted to the idea that if the parents so request – you can request for any school, mainstream school – to house the child, to provide education to the child, accept the child.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But when I went there, what I found was that, indeed, a child with special needs was in that school.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But I must say that the teacher was not well equipped, and the child was left pretty much alone.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: While SDSC currently has many sports under its umbrella, it has some advantages as well.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For example, when it is promoting sports to persons with special needs broadly, they can do so because resources are within them, the coaches are in their network.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When they want to organise a disability sports festival, they can do so with good effect.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we said in the speech, it is the interest of the athletes that we place front and foremost in our decision.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As we have seen in many cases, it can only go that much.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: They can also decide how they want to run the sports.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it has to be a partnership that we build up over the years.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The main consideration really is whether the interest of athletes with disabilities are better-served.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Can they be served in the mainstream so-called able-bodied NSAs?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: NSAs that have the capability, we would like to encourage them, we would like to work with them to make the change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But at the same time, we also need to consider all issues.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Also, we would like to mention that it is not just in high performance sports that we have an interest in getting into sports persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Very often, it is the ability to bring in a suite of activities that makes a lot of sense and provides value to the Special Education schools, because people like Whee Boon started with swimming, goes on to scuba-diving, and goes on to do rugby.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And the long or short of it is this: we are always looking at how to improve the system.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are making our facilities a lot more accessible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are offering more programmes so that more persons with disabilities can participate and we definitely want to support persons with disabilities like Ms Yip Pin Xiu and many other inspiring athletes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All of them, every single one of them, has inspiring life stories.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And they are such good role models for every one of us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We would like to support them, but we need to find the best modality.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are not starting from a blank canvas.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are starting with an existing set of organisations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, just let us move at the pace and the direction that are acceptable to all stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am totally convinced that MCCY, sports and the Government have become very inclusive.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I want to honour the Minister and the team for that.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I have seen it myself from the sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am just asking for, perhaps what Ms Yip Pin Xiu has been asking, just more re-imagination to have a continuum of operational models.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Some sports might be best left alone at the moment because of the nature of the game and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: But sports like running, even when someone is intellectually challenged, some of them may be able to run very, very fast and, together with the able-bodied athletes, can give them a run for their money.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I thought it would be good that as funders, the Government can stretch it a bit and get the funded bodies to re-imagine it a bit so that we can all join that conversation.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am not naive to think that everything should be inclusive, or everything should be just segregated but really looking at a blend.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: This is really part of how Singapore is currently proceeding as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Chairman, on behalf of the Government Parliamentary Committee as well as the 23 Members who have spoken in this discussion, I would like to thank the two Ministers, the two Senior Ministers of State as well as Minister of State and Senior Parliamentary Secretary for their answers for the 47 cuts that we have put in.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: I would also like to thank the women and men in MCCY and the related Statutory Boards for the steadfast and good work they have done in promoting a caring and cohesive society.
